It is ignored by the bedrock, vertex and foundry backends, which derive their own endpoints.

Give the whole prefix the endpoint expects, version segment included — "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1" rather than "https://openrouter.ai". The dialect appends only its own operation path to it.

Note that this field decides where conversation content is sent, so the permission to set it below tenant scope is granted rather than assumed.

identity.description:
Identity is the ExternalIdentity holding the credential presented to the provider — a BearerToken for an API key, an APIKey for gateways that want a named header such as Azure API Management's Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key, or a cloud identity for the bedrock, vertex and foundry backends.

The reserved value "ambient" means Wayfinder's own cloud credentials and is valid only on a system-scoped provider.

region.description: Region is the cloud region for the bedrock and vertex backends, e.g. "us-east-1" or "europe-west4".

resource.description: Resource is the Azure Foundry resource name, used to build its endpoint, e.g. "acme-ai-foundry".

headers.description: Headers are extra non-secret HTTP headers sent with every request, for gateways that want attribution or routing hints — OpenRouter's HTTP-Referer, for instance. Secret values belong in the ExternalIdentity named by Identity, never here: these are stored and returned in clear.

maxTokensField.description:
MaxTokensField names the request field this endpoint expects the output limit in. OpenAI-compatible servers disagree: the current field is maxCompletionTokens, which is the default here, but self-hosted runtimes and older gateways often accept only the original maxTokens and reject a request carrying the newer name.

Set it if the endpoint rejects requests with an unknown-field error mentioning max_completion_tokens. Applies to the openai dialect only.

enumDocs.description: Sends the limit as max_completion_tokens, which current OpenAI-compatible endpoints expect.
Sends the limit as max_tokens, the original field, which some self-hosted runtimes and older gateways require.

extraBody.description:
ExtraBody is merged into the JSON body of every request to this provider, for endpoints that need a field Wayfinder does not otherwise send. Its keys are the wire names the endpoint expects, and they overwrite anything Wayfinder set under the same name.

This is the escape hatch for an endpoint with its own requirements — a vendor-specific toggle, a routing hint, a sampling parameter — so that reaching one does not wait on Wayfinder adding a field for it. Nothing validates the contents beyond their being a JSON object: an endpoint that dislikes what you send will say so.

cost.description:
Cost declares what this provider's models cost.

Alpha: only Wayfinder's own system-scoped providers may set it, and it is rejected on a provider you define yourself. Inference on your own provider is billed by that provider and consumes no Wayfinder AI credits. You can read the weights on Wayfinder's providers to compare the relative cost of the models they offer.

unit.description: Unit is what the per-model weights are denominated in.

enumDocs.description: Denominates weights in Wayfinder AI credits, drawn against the tenant's plan allowance. Only a system-scoped provider may declare it.

models.description: Models is the catalogue this provider can run. Each entry maps a portable name, which is what an AIAgent references, onto the upstream model identifier this particular provider needs. The same "haiku-4.5" name can therefore be a public model ID on one provider and an account-specific inference-profile ARN on another, so retargeting an agent is a change of provider rather than an edit to every agent.

items.description: AIProviderModel is one model in a provider's catalogue.

name.description: Name is the portable name an AIAgent references, as the part after the ":" in an AIModelRef — "haiku-4.5" in "wayfinder/anthropic:haiku-4.5". Keep it the same across providers offering the same model so retargeting is a one-word change.

id.description: ID is the model identifier this provider's backend expects: a vendor model name, a Bedrock inference-profile ARN, an Azure Foundry deployment name, or a gateway slug such as "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5". Unlike Name it is free-form, because upstream identifiers routinely contain characters — slashes especially — that a reference grammar cannot carry.

displayName.description: DisplayName is the human-readable model name shown in the UI.

maxTokens.description:
MaxTokens is the largest number of tokens this model may generate in one reply. Set it to what the model actually supports: capacity varies by orders of magnitude between models, and a conversation that hits the limit is cut off mid-answer.

Left unset, a conservative default is applied, which for a large model wastes most of its capacity. An agent can still ask for less through its modelParameters, but it cannot exceed what the model can do, so this is the right place to record it.

thinking.description:
Thinking records how this model is asked to reason, so an agent can name an effort level without knowing which of the several ways to request it this particular model expects.

Leave it unset for a model that does no reasoning, or where the default behaviour is wanted and never varied.

mode.description: Mode is how this model is asked to reason. Getting it wrong is not a degraded result but a rejected request: a model configured by token budget refuses a request naming an effort level, and a current model refuses a token budget.

enumDocs.description: Asks for reasoning by naming a level, which is how current models are configured.
Asks for reasoning by giving a number of tokens to spend on it, which is how older models are configured. Those models reject a request that names a level instead, so the two are not interchangeable.
Describes a model that always reasons and cannot be asked not to. Effort still selects how deeply.

default.description: Default is the effort used when an agent names none.

enumDocs.description: Answers directly, without reasoning first.
Does a little reasoning — for short, scoped tasks where speed matters more than depth.
Balances reasoning depth against time and cost.
Reasons thoroughly — the right default for work where the answer's quality matters.
Reasons harder than high, for demanding coding and agentic work on models that offer the level.
Reasons as deeply as the model can, for problems where correctness matters more than what it costs.

min.description: Min is the least effort this model can be asked for. Set it on a model that always reasons, so that asking for none is raised to what it will actually do rather than being sent and refused.

enumDocs.description: Answers directly, without reasoning first.
Does a little reasoning — for short, scoped tasks where speed matters more than depth.
Balances reasoning depth against time and cost.
Reasons thoroughly — the right default for work where the answer's quality matters.
Reasons harder than high, for demanding coding and agentic work on models that offer the level.
Reasons as deeply as the model can, for problems where correctness matters more than what it costs.

max.description: Max is the most effort this model offers. A request for more is clamped to it, which is what lets an agent name a level that only some of its models can reach.

enumDocs.description: Answers directly, without reasoning first.
Does a little reasoning — for short, scoped tasks where speed matters more than depth.
Balances reasoning depth against time and cost.
Reasons thoroughly — the right default for work where the answer's quality matters.
Reasons harder than high, for demanding coding and agentic work on models that offer the level.
Reasons as deeply as the model can, for problems where correctness matters more than what it costs.

budgets.description: Budgets maps each effort level onto the number of thinking tokens to ask for, for a model in budget mode. A level with no entry falls back to the nearest lower level that has one.

levelNames.description: LevelNames renames a level for endpoints that spell it differently — a gateway calling the top level "xhigh" where the model itself calls it "max", for instance. Levels absent here are sent under their own name.

contextWindow.description: ContextWindow is the total number of tokens this model can consider at once, covering the conversation so far and the reply it is about to make. It is recorded for display and comparison — Wayfinder does not trim a conversation to fit it.

inputWeight.description: InputWeight is the cost of one input token, in Cost.Unit. Weights are per single token, so a model charged one credit per input token carries 1 here.

outputWeight.description: OutputWeight is the cost of one output token, in Cost.Unit.

cacheReadWeight.description: CacheReadWeight is the cost of one token read from the provider's prompt cache, in Cost.Unit.

cacheCreationWeight.description: CacheCreationWeight is the cost of one token written to the provider's prompt cache, in Cost.Unit.

kinds.description:
AISkill is markdown telling the assistant how to do one job — what the page a person is on is for, what to do and what to leave alone there, and which kinds of configuration a suggestion on it would be.

The assistant is told the name and description of every skill it can read, and the page a person is on can name the skill that covers it. The assistant reads a skill's body when it needs it, as the skill stands at that moment, so an edit applies from the next time a conversation reads it.

Wayfinder ships skills for its own pages, referenced as "wayfinder/NAME"; a tenant writes its own and references them by a bare name. A tenant's skill adds to the shipped ones and does not replace them: a tenant skill with the same name as a shipped one is a second, separate skill. Anyone signed in can read the shipped skills, e.g. with "wf get aiskills --scope system". A skill is held by the tenant, not by a workspace or an environment, and every AI user in the tenant can read it, so do not put anything in one that they should not see.

A skill is not an AIContext: a context is the standing background an agent starts with whatever it is doing, a skill is how to do the job the person came for.

spec.description: AISkillSpec is what the skill says and a line saying what it is for.

description.description: Description says which job this skill covers, e.g. "Who can do what in a workspace". The assistant reads it to decide whether to load the skill, so write it for that: name the job and the questions it answers.

markdown.description: Markdown is the body of the skill: what the page is for, what the assistant should do and not do there, and which resource kinds a suggestion on that page would be. The assistant reads the whole body when it loads the skill. It must be at most 64 KiB.

files.description: Files are further documents the assistant reads only when it needs one, e.g. one file for each cloud, so a conversation about AWS never reads the Azure detail. The body says what each file is for, and the assistant reads a file by its name. A skill may carry at most 16 files.

items.description: AISkillFile is one further document a skill carries, which the assistant reads on its own when the skill's body says it is needed.

name.description: Name is the name the body and the assistant use for the file, e.g. "aws.md". It is a single file name, not a path: at most 253 letters, digits, '-', '_' and '.', and unique within the skill.

markdown.description: Markdown is the content of the file. It must be at most 64 KiB.

tools.description: Tools are the tools this skill brings, in the same form as an agent's tools: each names a tool and gives any configuration that tool takes, e.g. {"name": "search_terraform_modules"}. When the assistant reads the skill it is told of each as a command of the skill, and runs one through run_skill_command. A tool runs with the conversation's own access, as it would if the agent held it, so a skill never lets the assistant do more than it already may. Only tools that run inside Wayfinder can be brought, not ones the chat client or the conversation's sandbox runs, and not the tools an agent holds itself: load_skill, run_skill_command, submit_changes and report_skill_result. The agent must hold run_skill_command to call them.

items.description: AgentTool selects a tool for an agent to use, with any configuration that tool takes.

name.description: Name is the tool's registered name, e.g. "validate_resource".

config.description: Config is tool-specific configuration, as a JSON object the tool interprets.

mcps.description: MCPs are the MCP servers this skill brings, in the same form as an agent's MCPs: each names an MCP and, optionally, which of its tools, e.g. {"mcp": "wayfinder/aws-knowledge", "toolScope": "selected", "tools": ["search_documentation", "read_documentation"]}. When the assistant reads the skill it is told each server's tools as commands, and it runs one through run_skill_command. A skill brings only a server that needs no credential, such as a public documentation server, so it passes the server no inputs. An MCP is "wayfinder/NAME" for one Wayfinder ships, or a bare "NAME" for one of your tenant's own. The agent must hold run_skill_command to call them.

items.description: AIAgentMCPBinding gives an agent access to one MCP server and limits which of that server's tools it may call. It is the agent side of the binding between an agent and an MCP; the MCP side, its spec.builtInAgents, lets a tenant's own MCP reach a built-in agent it cannot edit.

mcp.description: MCP is the scope-aware reference to the MCP server this binding exposes to the agent: "wayfinder/NAME" for one shipped with Wayfinder, a bare "NAME" for one of the tenant's own. A built-in agent may only reference "wayfinder/NAME".

toolScope.description: ToolScope selects whether the agent receives every tool the MCP server advertises ("all") or only the subset listed in tools ("selected"). An empty value is treated as "all".

enumDocs.description: Exposes every tool the MCP server advertises to the bound agent. It is the default when ToolScope is unset.
Exposes only the tools named in the binding's Tools list to the bound agent.

tools.description: Tools is the list of the server's tool names the agent may call. It applies only when toolScope is "selected", and must be empty when it is "all". A name the server no longer advertises is ignored.

inputs.description:
Inputs are the values this agent calls the MCP with, for the inputs the MCP declares. They take precedence over the MCP's own, so one MCP serves many agents instead of a copy per agent, each pointed at a different account.

This is also how an agent avoids a hardcoded credential. A value may read the agent's own inputs, e.g. "${{ .Inputs.ddCredential }}", so the identity comes from whoever starts the conversation — one they hold at their own workspace or environment and are permitted to use — rather than one baked into the agent that the caller may have no access to.

Whoever supplies an identity is checked against their own grant: a literal named here is checked when the agent is saved, a value supplied by a conversation when that conversation starts, and the resolved credential again when the call is made, so a grant withdrawn in between stops working.

items.description: TemplatedInput is a named input value, potentially containing template expressions.

name.description: Name matches a ValueDefinition on the associated plan.

value.description: Value is a literal value or template expression, resolved at reconciliation time. Stored as json.RawMessage so non-string types (numbers, bools) survive YAML round-trips without forced quoting. Template expressions like "${{ .Vars.x }}" are stored as JSON strings.

resultSchema.description: ResultSchema is the JSON Schema of what the job produces, when it hands back something it found rather than a change to make, e.g. a shortlist of modules: {"type": "object", "properties": {"candidates": {"type": "array", "items": {...}}}, "required": ["candidates"]}. The assistant is given it when it reads the skill, and hands the result back with report_skill_result, which refuses a result that does not match it. With a person in the conversation they are shown the result; with nobody there it becomes the conversation's result. It must describe an object, and be at most 16 KiB.

resultChoice.description: ResultChoice says the result is a choice for the person to make, and how to offer it: which list in the result holds the options, the label each is shown with, and the message sent for them when they pick one, e.g. {"items": "candidates", "label": "{source} {version}", "message": "Use {source} version {version}"}. What they pick reaches the assistant as their next message, as though they had typed it. It can also name the command whose output the options must come from, and how each option is shown. It needs resultSchema.

items.description: Items is where the options are in the result: the name of a list, or a path through objects to one with '.' between the names, e.g. "candidates" or "shortlist.modules". Each option is an object.

label.description: Label is what the person reads for each option, e.g. "{source} {version}".

message.description: Message is what is sent for the person when they pick an option, as their next message, e.g. "Use {source} version {version}".

from.description: From names the command whose output the options are chosen from, e.g. {"command": "search-terraform-modules", "list": "candidates", "key": ["source"]}. Each option must match an entry the command returned, and is shown with that entry's fields added, so the facts the person sees come from the command rather than from the assistant. An option that matches nothing is refused. The templates below can then name the entry's fields as well as the option's; where both have a field, the option's is used.

command.description: Command is one of the commands this skill's tools bring, by its command name, e.g. "search-terraform-modules" for the tool search_terraform_modules. The command's latest output in the conversation is the one used.

list.description: List is where the entries are in the command's output: the name of a list, or a path to one with '.' between the names, e.g. "candidates". A path through a list takes that name from each of its items, so "sources.candidates" is every source's candidates together.

key.description: Key names the fields an option and its entry must both hold, with equal values, e.g. ["source"], or ["chartName", "repoURL"] when a name alone is not unique. Each is a field of the options in the result.

title.description: Title is the heading each option is shown with, e.g. "{source}".

subtitle.description: Subtitle is a line shown under the title, e.g. "version {version} from {upstream}".

description.description: Description is a paragraph shown for each option, e.g. "{description}".

reason.description: Reason is why the assistant offers the option, e.g. "{reason}".

link.description: Link is a web address the person can open for each option, e.g. "{sourceRepoURL}". It is shown only when every field it names came from the command's entry, with the same value on the option if the option has it too, as a key field does, and it is an http or https address. So an address the assistant wrote itself is never a link. It needs from.

facts.description: Facts are labelled values shown for each option, e.g. {"label": "Downloads", "value": "{downloads}", "format": "number"}. A fact whose value is empty is left out.

items.description: AISkillResultChoiceFact is one labelled value shown for each option.

label.description: Label is the name the value is shown with, e.g. "Downloads".

value.description: Value is the value, written as the label is, e.g. "{downloads}".

format.description: Format says how the value is shown: "number" for a count, shown with digit grouping; "date" for a date and time, e.g. "2026-05-01T09:00:00Z"; or "percent" for a value from 0 to 1, shown as a whole percentage, e.g. 0.58 as "58%". Leave it out to show the value as it is.

badges.description: Badges are labels shown on an option when a field of it is true, e.g. {"label": "Verified", "when": "verified"}.

items.description: AISkillResultChoiceBadge is a label shown on an option when a field of it is true.

label.description: Label is what the badge reads, e.g. "Verified".

when.description: When is the field that must be true for the badge to show, e.g. "verified".

recommended.description: Recommended is where in the result the assistant names the option it recommends, as the value of the option's first from.key field, e.g. "recommended". The path is written as for items. That option is marked as recommended. It needs from.

handBack.description: HandBack says what a change from this skill's job must be, when the job makes a change rather than finding something, e.g. {"resources": {"kinds": ["CloudResourcePlan"], "exactly": 1}} or {"wayfinderYaml": true}. The assistant is given it when it reads the skill, and hands the change back as files with submit_changes, naming the skill. Files that are not what the skill says are refused, saying what the skill hands back and what arrived. It guides the assistant, and grants nothing: every resource handed back is still checked in full. Set resources, wayfinderYaml or both.

resources.description: Resources says which resources the change may hold. Leave it out when the change holds none.

kinds.description: Kinds are the kinds of resource the change may hold, each one you write as configuration, e.g. ["Environment", "Cluster"]. List what the skill's own body proposes, and no more.

exactly.description: Exactly is how many resources the change must hold, across all its files, e.g. 1 for a skill that makes one plan. Leave it out to allow any number.

wayfinderYaml.description: WayfinderYaml says the change may be a Wayfinder.yaml. It is checked as validate_wayfinder_yaml checks one when it is handed back.

otherFiles.description: OtherFiles says the change may also hold files that are neither resources nor a Wayfinder.yaml, e.g. a Helm chart. They are handed back as they are, unchecked.

kinds.description: ExternalIdentity represents credentials or configuration that grant Wayfinder access to an external system: a cloud account (an AWS account, Azure subscription, or GCP project), a source control provider, a container registry, or any other endpoint Wayfinder must authenticate to on your behalf. The type field selects what kind of access this is and, for cloud types, which cloud it reaches; the matching sub-block carries the identity's configuration and any secret material.

spec.description:
ExternalIdentitySpec describes what external system this identity reaches and how Wayfinder authenticates to it. Exactly one sub-block is populated, matching the family of the selected type.

An update must still carry the configuration its type requires. Leave a stored secret value blank to keep it, or supply one to rotate it, so a manifest kept in source control can change an identity's description, purposes and usableBy grants without the secret being to hand. Create the identity with its secret first: a blank secret is only accepted once there is a stored one to keep.

A BearerToken update with no token writes "bearerToken: {}". An empty block and an absent one are not the same: "bearerToken:" on its own is rejected, because the type requires that configuration. APIKey works differently — keep every header name whose stored value you want, since an omitted header is removed and at least one must remain.

type.description: Type selects what kind of external system this identity grants access to. It is self-describing: it fixes the cloud (if any) and the set of fields this identity must carry. It cannot be changed once set.

enumDocs.description: Is a static AWS IAM user access key/secret pair.
Is a static Azure app registration client secret.
Is a static GCP service account JSON key.
Is a keyless AWS IAM role assumed via Wayfinder's OIDC trust.
Is a keyless Azure service principal assumed via Wayfinder's OIDC trust.
Is a keyless GCP service account impersonated via Wayfinder's OIDC trust.
Is a username/password pair for an HTTP endpoint.
Is a TLS client certificate and private key.
Is a bearer token presented in the Authorization header.
Is one or more API-key headers, each a name and a secret value.
Is an OAuth2 client-credentials grant configuration.

description.description: Description is a human-facing explanation of what this identity is for.

service.description: Service is the external service this identity authenticates to, as a host or base URL (for example "api.example.com" or "https://api.example.com"). It is the target for the endpoint family of types (BasicAuth, TLSClientCert, BearerToken, APIKey, OAuth2ClientCredentials) and is required for those. It must be empty for cloud types, which target via cloudAccountRef. It is the endpoint-facing sibling of cloudAccountRef — the two are mutually-exclusive targets.

aws.description: AWS carries the configuration for an AWS identity (AWSIAMUserKey or AWSIAMRole).

account.description: Account is the AWS account this identity reaches, named by its account ID, e.g. "123456789012". The account must already have been added to your tenant — add it on the AWS integration first. It cannot be changed once set.

defaultRegion.description: DefaultRegion is the default AWS region Wayfinder will use for API calls against this account when no region is supplied by the operation. AWS requires a region to sign and route API requests, even for global services such as Route53, so this is required for all AWS identities. E.g. eu-west-2

roleARN.description: RoleARN is the ARN of the IAM role assumed via Wayfinder's OIDC trust (federated identities), e.g. "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/wayfinder".

userARN.description: UserARN is the ARN of the IAM user principal (static access key identities), e.g. "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:user/wayfinder".

accessKeyID.description: AccessKeyID is the IAM user access key ID (static access key identities).

secretAccessKey.description:
SecretAccessKey is the IAM user secret access key (static access key identities).

On update leave this blank to keep the stored value, or supply one to rotate it. A read never returns it, so an unmodified read-modify-write keeps the credential as it was.

azure.description: Azure carries the configuration for an Azure identity (AzureClientSecret or AzureServicePrincipal).

subscription.description: Subscription is the Azure subscription this identity reaches, named by its subscription ID, e.g. "72f988bf-86f1-41af-91ab-2d7cd011db47". The subscription must already have been added to your tenant — add it on the Azure integration first. It cannot be changed once set.

tenantID.description: TenantID is the Azure directory (tenant) this identity resides in, e.g. "72f988bf-86f1-41af-91ab-2d7cd011db47". Leave it unset and Wayfinder takes it from the subscription, which belongs to exactly one directory.

clientID.description: ClientID is the app registration client ID.

clientSecret.description:
ClientSecret is the app registration client secret (static identities).

On update leave this blank to keep the stored value, or supply one to rotate it. A read never returns it, so an unmodified read-modify-write keeps the credential as it was.

gcp.description: GCP carries the configuration for a GCP identity (GCPServiceAccountKey or GCPServiceAccount).

project.description: Project is the Google Cloud project this identity reaches, named by its project ID, e.g. "my-project". The project must already have been added to your tenant — add it on the Google Cloud integration first. It cannot be changed once set.

serviceAccount.description: ServiceAccount is the service account email this identity acts as, e.g. "wayfinder@my-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com".

serviceAccountKey.description:
ServiceAccountKey is the service account JSON key (static identities).

On update leave this blank to keep the stored value, or supply one to rotate it. A read never returns it, so an unmodified read-modify-write keeps the credential as it was.

projectNumber.description: ProjectNumber is the numerical ID Google assigned the project, e.g. "123456789012". Required when accessing GCP from outside GCP (e.g. via Wayfinder OIDC). Leave it unset and Wayfinder takes it from the project, which is where it is recorded.

workloadIdentityPoolID.description: WorkloadIdentityPoolID is the ID of the workload identity pool to use for this project. Required when accessing GCP from outside GCP (e.g. via Wayfinder OIDC) From the GCP validation: "This value can contain the characters a–z and 0–9.", "Must be at least 4 characters long."

workloadIdentityProviderID.description: WorkloadIdentityProviderID is the ID of the workload identity provider to use for this project. Required when accessing GCP from outside GCP (e.g. via Wayfinder OIDC) From the GCP validation: "This value can contain the characters a–z and 0–9.", "Must be at least 4 characters long."

basicAuth.description: BasicAuth carries a username and password for an HTTP endpoint.

password.description:
Password is the basic-auth password.

On update leave this blank to keep the stored value, or supply one to rotate it. A read never returns it, so an unmodified read-modify-write keeps the credential as it was.

tls.description: TLS carries a TLS client certificate and private key.

cert.description: Cert is the PEM-encoded TLS client certificate.

key.description:
Key is the PEM-encoded TLS client private key.

On update leave this blank to keep the stored value, or supply one to rotate it. A read never returns it, so an unmodified read-modify-write keeps the credential as it was.

bearerToken.description: BearerToken carries a bearer token presented in the Authorization header.

token.description:
Token is the bearer token.

On update leave this blank to keep the stored value, or supply one to rotate it. A read never returns it, so an unmodified read-modify-write keeps the credential as it was.

apiKey.description: APIKey carries the API-key headers presented to the endpoint, keyed by header name.

headers.description:
Headers maps each HTTP header name to the secret value sent in it, for example {"X-API-Key": "..."}. Most APIs take one header; some require several — Datadog wants both DD-API-KEY and DD-APPLICATION-KEY — so all of them belong to one identity rather than being split across several. Header names are stored in clear, so you can see how the identity presents itself; the values are stored encrypted and never returned by the API.

On update the map you send is the complete set of headers: leave a value blank to keep the stored one, supply a value to rotate it, and omit a header entirely to remove it. Since a read returns the header names with their values blanked, an unmodified read-modify-write keeps every credential as it was.

oauth2.description: OAuth2 carries an OAuth2 client-credentials grant configuration.

tokenURL.description: TokenURL is the OAuth2 token endpoint the client-credentials grant is exchanged at.

clientID.description: ClientID is the OAuth2 client identifier.

scopes.description: Scopes are the OAuth2 scopes requested for the minted access token.

clientSecret.description:
ClientSecret is the OAuth2 client secret.

On update leave this blank to keep the stored value, or supply one to rotate it. A read never returns it, so an unmodified read-modify-write keeps the credential as it was.

cloudAccountRef.description: CloudAccountRef identifies the account, subscription or project this identity reaches, as "<cloud>:<identifier>". It is derived from the identifier in the cloud sub-block and is not set directly by users; the object it names must already have been added to the tenant. It is empty for non-cloud (credential) identities.

usableFor.description: UsableFor states what this identity is for: the kinds of use it may ever be put to, such as provisioning infrastructure, managing DNS, or fetching Helm charts. It is a property of the credential itself, true before anyone is granted anything, and no grant can name a verb that is not here — a use is permitted only when the verb appears here and the caller holds it through usableBy. It is required when the identity is created, and the values it accepts are constrained by the identity's type: an APIKey credential cannot provision infrastructure.

enumDocs.description: Lets this identity be used to provision infrastructure through Wayfinder's provisioning engine, such as a cloud resource or a stack instance target.
Lets this identity be used to discover, import and reach managed Kubernetes clusters in the account it targets.
Lets this identity be used to manage DNS zones and records in the account it targets.
Lets this identity be used to reach an AI inference provider, either a cloud-hosted model service or a direct endpoint that takes an inference key.
Lets this identity be used to fetch infrastructure modules from a private registry or source repository.
Lets this identity be used to fetch Helm charts from a private chart repository, and to search one for charts.
Lets this identity be used to authenticate outbound calls to a web API integration.
Lets this identity be used to authenticate connections to an MCP server integration.
Lets a subject obtain this identity's credentials and wield them directly, rather than having Wayfinder use them on their behalf.

usableBy.description: UsableBy lists who may use this identity and for what. Each entry names either a subject or a Wayfinder role held at a scope, plus the verbs granted to it. A grant that lists no verbs is granted everything in usableFor, and follows it as it changes; a grant that lists verbs explicitly may only list ones that appear in usableFor.

items.description: ExternalIdentityUsableBy grants a set of use verbs over an external identity to a grantee. The grantee is either an explicit subject or a Wayfinder role held at a scope — exactly one of subject or role must be set.

subject.description: Subject is the user, service account or group this grant is for. Exactly one of subject or role must be set.

role.description: Role grants use to any subject holding a Wayfinder role at a scope, evaluated from the roles the caller holds at the time of the request. Its scope fields are read relative to where the identity itself lives: workspace is pinned for a workspace-scoped identity, both are pinned for an environment-scoped one, and a tenant-scoped identity must state one or the other. Exactly one of subject or role must be set.
Role is the name of the Wayfinder role whose holders are granted, e.g. "deployer", "viewer" or "workspace.manager".

workspace.description: Workspace is the workspace holders must hold the role in. "*" matches any workspace. It is inert where the granting resource pins a workspace of its own, and is mutually exclusive with tenant.

environment.description: Environment narrows the grant to holders of the role in a single environment. Leave it empty to require the role at workspace scope and nothing narrower, or set "*" to match the role held at workspace scope or in any one environment. It is inert where the granting resource pins an environment of its own, and has no meaning alongside tenant, which names a scope no environment sits under.

tenant.description: Tenant grants to holders of the role at tenant scope, such as "tenant.owner" - a tenant-level role holding rather than one held in any particular workspace, so the two never match the same people. It may only be set where the granting resource reaches the whole tenant, and is mutually exclusive with workspace.

verbs.description: Verbs are the use verbs this grantee is granted over the identity. Leaving it empty grants every verb in spec.usableFor, and keeps following that list as it changes — it does NOT confer nothing. List verbs explicitly to grant a narrower set; each one must already appear in spec.usableFor, since a grant can never reach beyond what the identity is for.

enumDocs.description: Lets this identity be used to provision infrastructure through Wayfinder's provisioning engine, such as a cloud resource or a stack instance target.
Lets this identity be used to discover, import and reach managed Kubernetes clusters in the account it targets.
Lets this identity be used to manage DNS zones and records in the account it targets.
Lets this identity be used to reach an AI inference provider, either a cloud-hosted model service or a direct endpoint that takes an inference key.
Lets this identity be used to fetch infrastructure modules from a private registry or source repository.

It may be nothing else: it names a Wayfinder object, so it has to resolve without running the call — that is what lets the identity be permission-checked when you save, and what keeps it visible to "what breaks if I delete this credential?".

codeRepoRef.description:
CodeRepoRef names the repository each call works on. Requests are authenticated with a short-lived token that Wayfinder mints for that repository alone, through the App it holds for the repository's provider. No secret is stored. Mutually exclusive with ExternalIdentityRef.

It is always a whole-field "${{ .Inputs.<name> }}" expression naming an input of kind CodeRepo, e.g. "${{ .Inputs.codeRepo }}", never a literal, so the repository is chosen by whatever uses the connection: an AI conversation answers it with the repository in its source context, and a web API invocation with one of its inputs. A call is refused unless the user, agent or workflow it is made for holds the access it needs in the repository's usableBy. Only GitHub repositories are supported.

access.description: Access is the most an MCP's calls may do in the repository CodeRepoRef names: "read" (the default) or "write". A call is made at the highest level up to this that the conversation asked for and its agent holds. A web API takes the level from each operation's method instead — "read" for GET and HEAD, "write" otherwise — and refuses this field.

enumDocs.description: Clones and fetches the repository and reads its CI results — which workflow run failed, which check is red, and what has been deployed.
Additionally pushes branches, opens pull requests and comments on them.

githubOrgRef.description:
GitHubOrgRef named the GitHub organisation a connection signed in to.

Deprecated: replaced by codeRepoRef. A connection that still sets it cannot be saved, and its calls are refused.

headers.description:
Headers are sent on every request, in addition to anything an individual operation adds. Values may be literals or expressions over the declared inputs. Do not set a credential header here — Auth applies the credential by its type, and a header set by hand bypasses that.

On an MCP a value may also read the arguments of the tool call it is sent with, as "${{ .Args.<name> }}", so one registration serves every repository or project an agent asks about instead of one per value. GitHub's hosted Actions server wants "Mcp-Param-owner" and "Mcp-Param-repo" that way: with "${{ .Args.owner }}" the agent passes owner and repo in the tool call, as the tool's own schema asks, and the call works. A header reading an argument the call did not carry is left off, so the server answers saying which value it wanted rather than acting on a blank one. A WebAPI has no such arguments and refuses the expression.

operations.description: Operations are the templated HTTP operations exposed by this WebAPI. Each has a unique name and is invoked to produce a WebAPIInvocation.

items.description: WebAPIOperation defines a single templated HTTP operation on a WebAPI.

name.description: Name is the unique identifier for this operation within the WebAPI.

summary.description: Summary is a short description of what this operation does.

method.description: Method is the HTTP method (GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE).

path.description: Path is the URL path appended to the connection's base URL, e.g. "/repos/${{ .Inputs.owner }}/${{ .Inputs.repo }}/issues". Input values are substituted per invocation.

headers.description: Headers are additional headers for this operation. Values support Go templating.

body.description: Body is the request body template. Supports Go templating.

inputs.description: Inputs defines the input schema for this operation — what inputs it expects.

items.description: ValueDefinition defines the shape of an input/output/data value

name.description: Name of the variable

description.description: Description iof the value

secret.description: Secret indicates if the value is a secret and should be protected

type.description: Type is the type of the value

enumDocs.description: Is a string type
Is a number type (integer or floating point)
Is a boolean type
Is a list type of strings
Is a list type of numbers
Is a list type of booleans
Is a map type of strings
Is a map type of numbers
Is a map type of booleans
Is an arbitrary JSON type, used to represent any complex input/output that isn't better represented by the other types. Note that no validation is possible for a plain JSON input.

Is a reference to an ExternalIdentity, naming the credential an outbound call authenticates with. The value is the identity's name and the scope it lives at ("my-identity", "my-workspace/my-identity" or "my-workspace/my-env/my-identity"), never credential material itself. Supplying a value resolves it: the identity must exist, you must be allowed to use it for what is calling, and its own kind must be one the definition's identityTypes accepts. A value naming an identity that fails any of those is refused when it is supplied, rather than failing when the call runs. It may only be declared where a definition is able to load an identity. It is refused on a CloudResourcePlan's inputs and outputs, a KubeResourcePlan's inputs, a stack definition's vars, an IntegrationDefinition's paramDefs, and a repo template's inputs, all of which would otherwise receive the reference as a plain string.

Is a reference to a CodeRepo, naming the repository an AI agent works on. The value names the repository as its provider does, "github.com/OWNER/REPO" (e.g. "github.com/appvia/wayfinder"), never a URL or a git credential. Use it on an AI agent's input where the repository is not fixed when the agent is written: the input sets how much of the repository the agent needs (repoAccess) and the branch prefix for its changes (repoBranchPrefix), and whoever starts the conversation supplies the repository. The conversation's spec.sourceContext is built from the value they supply. Supplying a value resolves it: the repository must exist, and the grant in its usableBy must cover the access the input asks for. That grant is checked against the person supplying the repository, not against whoever wrote the agent. The agent is checked separately, against the same repository, when the conversation is created. It may only be declared where a definition is able to load a repository and check that grant. It is refused on a CloudResourcePlan's and a KubeResourcePlan's inputs and outputs, a stack definition's vars, an IntegrationDefinition's paramDefs, and a repo template's inputs: each of those passes its values through as text to Terraform, a Helm chart, a rendered manifest or a scaffolded file, where the reference is only a plain string and no grant over the repository is checked.

optional.description: Optional is true when no value need be supplied: the object declaring it can be saved, and switched on where it has a switch, without one. An unanswered optional value reads as its defaultValue when one is set, and as nothing otherwise. Whether whoever uses the object may supply it later is for that object to say.

minimum.description: Minimum is the minimum numerical value of the variable if a number/float

maximum.description: Maximum is the maximum numerical value of the variable if a number/float

minLength.description: MinLength is the minimum number or length of the variable if a string

maxLength.description: MaxLength is the maximum number or length of the variable if a string

minItems.description: MinItems is the minimum number of items in the variable if a list or map

maxItems.description: MaxItems is the maximum number of items in the variable if a list or map

pattern.description: Pattern is the pattern of the variable if a string. For list(string) and map(string), this is applied to each individual value in the list or map.

enum.description: Enum is the list of valid values for a string or number (or the values of lists/maps of those types). Ignored for other types.

requiredKeys.description: RequiredKeys is the list of required keys for a map variable. Ignored for other types.

refType.description: RefType describes that this value is a reference to another Wayfinder resource. When set, the value is validated to be the name of an existing resource of the given kind, optionally filtered by field constraints.

kind.description: Kind is the Wayfinder resource kind being referenced (e.g. "ExternalIdentity", "CodeRepo")

filter.description: Filter is an optional set of dot-path field matchers on the referenced resource. Keys are dot-paths (e.g. "spec.cloud"), values are the expected string match. All entries must match (AND semantics).

identityTypes.description: IdentityTypes lists the ExternalIdentity types this input accepts, e.g. ["BearerToken"] for an API that authenticates with a bearer token, or ["BasicAuth", "BearerToken"] where either will do. A value naming an identity of any other type is refused when it is supplied, rather than failing when the call runs. Leaving it empty accepts any identity type that can authenticate an outbound call. It may be set only on type=externalidentity, and is refused on every other type.

repoAccess.description: RepoAccess is how much of the repository the agent needs: "read" to clone and read it, "propose" to also commit to a fresh branch and open a pull request, or "proposeWorkflows" to also change the repository's CI workflow definitions. When empty, Wayfinder uses "read". Whoever supplies a repository must themselves be granted at least this much of it, and so must the agent, or the conversation is refused when it is created. It may be set only on type=coderepo, and is refused on every other type.

repoBranchPrefix.description: RepoBranchPrefix is prepended to the name of the branch the agent's changes are committed to, e.g. "wayfinder-ai/cost-control/". When empty, branches are prefixed "wayfinder-ai/". Set it so branch protection or CODEOWNERS rules in the repository match every branch this agent opens; whoever starts the conversation cannot change it. It may be set only on type=coderepo, and is refused on every other type.

schema.description: Schema provides additional guidance as to the shape of the value when type=json.

response.description: Response defines how to handle the response from this operation.

successCondition.description: SuccessCondition is a JQ boolean expression over the response that must evaluate to true for the call to be a success (e.g. `.statusCode == 200`). When empty the default is a 2xx status. A result that is not a boolean is a configuration error (reason=condition-error), not a silent failure.

store.description: Store defines the response data to extract (via JQ) and store as ResourceData on the target resource.

dataType.description: DataType references the DataType resource whose schema validates the extracted Values. Its name — without any workspace prefix — is the key the data is stored under on the target resource. A bare name is the tenant's shared type, e.g. "incident"; "workspace/name" is one that workspace defined for itself, e.g. "team-a/incident". There is no fallback between the two, so a bare name always means the shared type. Only this web API's own workspace may be named: a tenant-scoped web API can use the shared types alone, and none can reach into another workspace. When set, Values must also be set (typed mode). When unset, the mode depends on Values: empty Values stores the response body verbatim (raw mode); non-empty Values extracts just those named fields with no schema (extraction-only mode).

values.description: Values is a map of output-field name → JQ expression, e.g. {"issueNumber": ".body.number"}, evaluated against the response context (`.statusCode`, `.body`, `.headers`) to build the object of extracted fields. Required when DataType is set (typed, validated). Optional when DataType is empty: set it to expose named fields without a schema, or leave it empty to store the whole body (raw mode).

itemsToParse.description:
ItemsToParse, when set, is a JQ expression yielding an array within the response, e.g. `.body.projects` for an endpoint that returns one entry per service. The store is then applied once per element, with the element exposed as `.item`, so a single call can write to many resources. Leave it empty when the response describes a single thing.

A polled endpoint nearly always returns a collection, so this is how a scheduled call spreads its results across the resources they belong to.

resource.description:
Resource selects which Wayfinder resource(s) the extracted data is stored against, by matching values pulled out of the response.

Leave it unset for a call made in the context of something — a workflow step or a stack hook — where the data belongs to whatever triggered it. Set it for a call with no such context, above all a scheduled one: the data belongs to the resource it is *about*, not to the WebAPI that fetched it, and nothing else can work that out.

kind.description: Kind is the Wayfinder kind(s) to match — accepts a single kind name (`kind: StackInstance`) or a list of kinds (`kind: [StackInstance, KubeResource]`) to broadcast across kinds. Required once a data mapping is configured (enforced by validation); an endpoint-only webhook has no mapping.

workspace.description: Workspace is a JQ expression over the payload yielding the workspace to match, e.g. `.body.labels.workspace`. Omit to match any workspace.

environment.description: Environment is a JQ expression over the payload yielding the environment to match, e.g. `.body.labels.environment`. Omit to match any environment.

name.description: Name is a JQ expression over the payload yielding the resource name to match exactly, e.g. `.body.labels.app`. Omit to match any name.

labels.description: Labels is a map of label key → JQ expression, e.g. {"team": ".body.commonLabels.team"}. Each entry adds a label the target resource must carry with the resulting value.

onMultiMatch.description: OnMultiMatch controls behaviour when the query returns >1 match. "all" (default) writes to every match; "first" picks the alphabetically first.

enumDocs.description: Writes the mapped data to every matched resource.
Writes only to the alphabetically first match.

schedules.description:
Schedules call operations automatically on a repeating interval, for sources that have no webhook and must be polled — cloud cost, seat and usage metrics, or a periodic posture snapshot.

Deliberately separate from the operations themselves: WHAT an operation does is one thing, and WHEN to run it is another. The same operation can be scheduled more than once at different intervals with different inputs (this month's costs hourly, last month's daily), and an operation with no schedule is not a lesser kind of operation — it simply runs when a workflow, a stack hook or a person asks.

Each entry maintains a Schedule resource, kept in step by writing this spec. Those Schedules are read-only: change them here.

items.description: WebAPISchedule calls one of the WebAPI's operations on a repeating interval.

name.description:
Name identifies this schedule within the WebAPI, and is what the Schedule resource is named after. Defaults to the operation name, which is all you need when an operation is scheduled once; name it explicitly to schedule the same operation more than once — this month's costs hourly and last month's daily, say.

It is the schedule's identity, so it is also what its run history hangs off: changing the interval of a named schedule adjusts that schedule, whereas renaming it starts a new one.

operation.description: Operation names which of this WebAPI's operations to call. It must be one the spec declares.

every.description: Every is how long to wait between calls, e.g. "15m", "1h" or "24h". Pick a value comfortably longer than the call itself takes, and be mindful of what is at the other end: a slow daily report does not want a five-minute interval.

inputs.description: Inputs are the values to call the operation with, validated against what it declares it accepts. A scheduled call has nobody to ask, so anything the operation needs has to be settled here: a query parameter, a lookback window, a page size. An operation that requires inputs cannot be scheduled without them.

items.description: TemplatedInput is a named input value, potentially containing template expressions.

name.description: Name matches a ValueDefinition on the associated plan.

value.description: Value is a literal value or template expression, resolved at reconciliation time. Stored as json.RawMessage so non-string types (numbers, bools) survive YAML round-trips without forced quoting. Template expressions like "${{ .Vars.x }}" are stored as JSON strings.

suspend.description: Suspend stops this schedule running without removing it, so it can be switched back on without losing the record of when it last ran.

kinds.description: Webhook accepts signed HTTP POST deliveries from an external system at a secret ingest URL, and writes data extracted from each delivery onto the Wayfinder resources it matches. The signature, target-resource query and the values to store are all configured on the spec; every delivery is recorded as a WebhookInvocation.

spec.description: WebhookSpec defines the desired configuration of a Webhook: how inbound deliveries are verified, and what data they write where.

description.description: Description is a short description of what this webhook is for.

integrationRef.description: IntegrationRef is the integration this webhook belongs to, e.g. "github" or "team-a/github". Required: every webhook is owned by an integration, which must already exist and cannot be deleted while this webhook exists. The reference says where the integration lives, independent of where the webhook lives — a bare "name" is a tenant-scoped (shared) integration, "workspace/name" is a workspace-scoped one — so a workspace webhook may reference a shared tenant integration by bare name. It is blank only in a catalogue definition's template, where Wayfinder fills it in when you install the integration.

enabled.description: Enabled toggles whether this webhook accepts inbound deliveries. A disabled webhook rejects deliveries (recording the rejection) but keeps its ingest URL and configuration. Omitted means enabled — an explicit false is required to turn a webhook off. Webhooks created from a catalogue entry start disabled; turn them on once configured.

definitionRef.description: DefinitionRef records the catalogue entry this webhook came from, as "<definition>@<generation>", e.g. "wayfinder.github@3". Set by Wayfinder when you install an integration from the catalogue; empty for webhooks you create directly. Read-only.

security.description: Security defines how inbound deliveries are authenticated and what HMAC algorithm/secret/header signals are expected.

algorithm.description: Algorithm is the HMAC algorithm the upstream uses to sign the body. "none" means URL secrecy only — accepted but not recommended for any payload an attacker could mint.

enumDocs.description: Verifies deliveries with an HMAC-SHA256 signature of the request body (e.g. GitHub's X-Hub-Signature-256).
Verifies deliveries with an HMAC-SHA1 signature of the request body.
Performs no signature verification, relying on the secrecy of the ingest URL alone. Not recommended for any payload an attacker could mint.

secret.description: Secret is the shared HMAC signing secret used to verify inbound delivery signatures. Required unless Algorithm is "none". Stored encrypted at rest and never returned by the API — supply it to set or rotate it, leave it blank on update to keep the stored value.

signatureHeader.description: SignatureHeader is the HTTP header the upstream uses to carry the signature (e.g. "X-Hub-Signature-256"). Required unless Algorithm is "none".

signaturePrefix.description: SignaturePrefix is stripped from the header value before comparison (e.g. "sha256=" for GitHub).

requestIdHeader.description: RequestIDHeader is the upstream's per-delivery unique ID header (e.g. X-GitHub-Delivery). Enables short-window dedup.

storage.description: Storage defines what each delivery writes and where. Every delivery is applied to every entry, and each entry selects its own target resources, splits its own batched items and writes its own data entry. Optional: a webhook with no storage still records every delivery without writing to any resource, which lets you confirm connectivity and inspect real payloads before deciding what to store.

items.description: WebhookResourceData is one storage configuration: which resources a delivery targets, what data is written on each of them, and how a batched body is split into individual items for this configuration.

itemsToParse.description: ItemsToParse, when set, is a JQ expression yielding an array within the delivery, e.g. `.body.alerts` for a sender that batches several alerts into one POST. This configuration is then applied once per element, with the element exposed as `.item`. Leave it empty when each delivery carries a single record.

resource.description: Resource defines the query that selects the target resource(s) for this delivery.

kind.description: Kind is the Wayfinder kind(s) to match — accepts a single kind name (`kind: StackInstance`) or a list of kinds (`kind: [StackInstance, KubeResource]`) to broadcast across kinds. Required once a data mapping is configured (enforced by validation); an endpoint-only webhook has no mapping.

workspace.description: Workspace is a JQ expression over the payload yielding the workspace to match, e.g. `.body.labels.workspace`. Omit to match any workspace.

environment.description: Environment is a JQ expression over the payload yielding the environment to match, e.g. `.body.labels.environment`. Omit to match any environment.

name.description: Name is a JQ expression over the payload yielding the resource name to match exactly, e.g. `.body.labels.app`. Omit to match any name.

labels.description: Labels is a map of label key → JQ expression, e.g. {"team": ".body.commonLabels.team"}. Each entry adds a label the target resource must carry with the resulting value.

onMultiMatch.description: OnMultiMatch controls behaviour when the query returns >1 match. "all" (default) writes to every match; "first" picks the alphabetically first.

enumDocs.description: Writes the mapped data to every matched resource.
Writes only to the alphabetically first match.

data.description: Data defines the DataType and JQ-mapped values written against the matched resource(s).

dataType.description: DataType references the DataType resource whose schema validates the mapped Values. Its name — without any workspace prefix — is the key the data is stored under on the target resource. A bare name is the tenant's shared type, e.g. "incident"; "workspace/name" is one that workspace defined for itself, e.g. "team-a/incident". There is no fallback between the two, so a bare name always means the shared type. Only this webhook's own workspace may be named: a tenant-scoped webhook can use the shared types alone, and no webhook can reach into another workspace. When set, Values must also be set (typed mode). When unset, the webhook runs in raw mode: the inbound body is stored verbatim under dataKey=<webhook name> with no schema check and no JQ extraction.

values.description: Values is a map of stored-field name → JQ expression, e.g. {"severity": ".body.status"}. Each expression is evaluated against the delivery to build the object that is stored. Required when DataType is set; must be empty when DataType is empty.

keepHistory.description: KeepHistory controls write semantics. false (default) means each delivery overwrites the entry in place. true increments the generation and retains prior values as an audit trail.

maxPayloadBytes.description: MaxPayloadBytes caps the size of an inbound body, e.g. 1048576 for 1 MiB. Deliveries larger than this are rejected with HTTP 413.

kinds.description: KubeResource is a deployment of packaged software — a Helm chart and/or a set of Kubernetes manifests — into a namespace of a target cluster. It is normally created from a KubeResourcePlan, supplying the inputs that plan declares; the chart and manifests may also be given directly on the resource where no plan is used. Wayfinder renders the plan's templates, installs or upgrades the release in the cluster, creates any workload identity the plan asks for, and records the rendered values, applied manifests, produced outputs and rollout progress in the status.

spec.description: KubeResourceSpec defines the desired deployment of a Helm chart and/or Kubernetes manifests into a cluster namespace.

stackInstanceRef.description: StackInstanceRef is the stack instance this deployment belongs to, when it was created as part of an application deployment. It determines the template context available to the chart values and manifest templates.

name.description: Name is the object name of the referenced stack instance

workspace.description: Workspace identifies the workspace in which this item exists. If empty, assume the same workspace as the object holding the reference.

environment.description: Environment identifies the environment in which this item exists.

clusterRef.description: ClusterRef is the cluster this deployment is installed into.

workspace.description: Workspace identifies the workspace in which this item exists. If empty, assume the same workspace as the object holding the reference.

environment.description: Environment identifies the environment in which this item exists.

name.description: Name is the object name of the referenced item

deploymentRoles.description: DeploymentRoles are the Kubernetes ClusterRoles used to perform the deployment in the target cluster. Each must already exist in that cluster as a ClusterRole, and must be available to you through the cluster's spec.access configuration.

items.description: KubeResourceDeploymentRole names a Kubernetes ClusterRole in the target cluster to deploy with, and how it should be bound.

clusterRoleName.description: ClusterRoleName is the name of the ClusterRole in the target cluster to deploy with, e.g. "cluster-admin".

roleBindingType.description: RoleBindingType is how the ClusterRole is bound for the deployment, either Cluster or Namespace. Namespace binds it only within the install namespace. If unspecified, Namespace is assumed.

enumDocs.description: Creates RoleBindings in specific namespaces
Creates ClusterRoleBindings for cluster-wide access

inputs.description: Inputs are the values supplied for the inputs the referenced plan declares, together with the environment the deployment belongs to and any dependencies it must wait for. Input values may be literals or template expressions, e.g. "${{ .Vars.dbHost }}", and resolve against the variable and secret hierarchy (tenant > workspace > environment).

values.description: Values are named input values matching the plan's ValueDefinitions. May contain template expressions (e.g. "${{ .Vars.name }}", "${{ .Secrets.key }}"). Resolved when Wayfinder applies the configuration — secret values are never stored here.

items.description: TemplatedInput is a named input value, potentially containing template expressions.

name.description: Name matches a ValueDefinition on the associated plan.

value.description: Value is a literal value or template expression, resolved at reconciliation time. Stored as json.RawMessage so non-string types (numbers, bools) survive YAML round-trips without forced quoting. Template expressions like "${{ .Vars.x }}" are stored as JSON strings.

planRef.description: PlanRef is the kube resource plan this deployment is created from, optionally pinned to a version, e.g. "nginx-ingress" or "nginx-ingress:2".

installNamespace.description: InstallNamespace is the namespace in the target cluster to install into, e.g. "ingress". Always required on a KubeResource.

helm.description: Helm is the Helm chart to install, and the values to install it with.

chartURL.description: ChartURL is the URL to a specific tarball of the helm chart. Must specify either ChartURL, or RepoUrl/RepoRef with ChartName and ChartVersion. Cannot be combined with ChartData (on KubeResourcePlan) or ChartPath (on Stack Components).

repoURL.description: RepoURL is a URL to a helm repository, either HTTP or OCI, e.g. "https://charts.example.com" or "oci://registry.example.com/charts". Must be combined with ChartName and ChartVersion. Cannot be combined with ChartURL, ChartData (on KubeResourcePlan), or ChartPath (on Stack Components). If RepoRef is also provided, this must point to the same URL as the referenced Repository.

repoRef.description: RepoRef is a reference to a Repository resource to use for the chart repo. If provided, the referenced Repository resource must reference the same URL as the RepoUrl field. Must be combined with ChartName and ChartVersion.

chartName.description: ChartName is the name of the chart to install. Required when using RepoUrl/RepoRef. Not required when using ChartURL or ChartData.

chartVersion.description: ChartVersion is the version of the chart to install, e.g. "4.11.2". Required when using RepoUrl/RepoRef. Not required when using ChartURL or ChartData.

valuesTemplate.description:
ValuesTemplate is a template containing the values to use when installing the Helm chart.

WF CLI supports a single file include directive in place of a string here when processing a KubeResourcePlan resource using wf apply (or wf validate kuberesourceplan). Use "!file filename" to load the content from a file with the relative path "filename".

helmTimeout.description: HelmTimeout is the duration to wait for helm install/upgrade operations to complete. If unspecified, the default timeout of 300s will be used. Must be a valid duration string (e.g. "600s", "10m").

skipTests.description: SkipTests will skip execution of any 'helm test' tests defined on the package. Defaults to false.

dryRun.description: DryRun will carry out a helm dry run step before installing or upgrading, to catch problems before anything is changed in the cluster. It is opt-in because a dry run fails for charts whose resources depend on custom resource definitions the chart itself installs. Defaults to false.

releaseName.description: ReleaseName is the name of the release in the cluster. If not specified, the KubeResource name will be used.

chartData.description: ChartData is the raw data of the helm chart. It is a base64 encoded string of a helm chart tar.gz file. Cannot be combined with ChartURL, RepoUrl/RepoRef, or ChartVersion.

additionalValuesFiles.description: AdditionalValuesFiles is a list of additional value files to apply when installing the Helm chart. These will be applied in the order specified after the values template, so can override values from the template. Do not include secret data in these files as they are handled in plain text. These additional files do NOT support templating, all templating should be performed in the ValuesTemplate.

manifests.description: Manifests are Kubernetes manifests to apply to the cluster, applied in the order given.

items.description: Manifest is a single Kubernetes manifest, given as a template, that is applied to the target cluster as part of the deployment.

name.description: Name is an optional name for this manifest. This name is used only for your reference and has no meaning to Wayfinder.

template.description:
Template is the Kubernetes manifest to apply, as a YAML template. It may use template expressions, e.g. "${{ .Cluster.Name }}".

WF CLI supports a single file include directive in place of a string here when processing a KubeResourcePlan resource using wf apply (or wf validate kuberesourceplan). Use "!file filename" to load the content from a file with the relative path "filename". If "!file" is used without a file, the manifest name will be used as the file name.

preInstall.description: PreInstall applies this manifest before the Helm chart is installed, rather than after. Use it for anything the chart itself depends on. Defaults to false.

kubeResourceType.description: KubeResourceType describes what this plan is suitable for, either AppComponent or ClusterWide. If unspecified, AppComponent is assumed.

enumDocs.description: Is a plan installed alongside applications, in their own namespaces. It can be installed many times per cluster, and suits things applications depend on directly, such as a database or a message queue.
Is a plan installed once per cluster, providing cluster-wide capability such as an operator, ingress controller or monitoring agent.

workloadIdentity.description: WorkloadIdentity requests a cloud identity for the workload this plan deploys, so it can access cloud resources without long-lived credentials.

serviceAccountName.description: ServiceAccountName is the name of the service account in the installNamespace which will use this identity in the target cluster.

identityOnly.description:
IdentityOnly will create an identity associated with a cluster with no specific permissions Must specify Role=None if this is true. In AWS:
  - An IAM role is created and associated with a specific Kubernetes service account
  - no inline or attached policies are managed (post creation of the IAM role)
  - It is a "user" responsibility to attach policies to the IAM role
In Azure:
  - The user defined managed identity is created
  - No role definitions or role assignments are created
  - It is a "user" responsibility to create relevant role assignments

role.description: Role allows the permissions of a workload identity to be specified

aws.description: AWS holds parameters specific to an AWS workload identity IRSA role

iamPolicyARNs.description:
IAMPolicyARNs defines a list of IAM policies to bind to the workload identity role These must exist in the target AWS account. E.g. arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/aws-service-role/AccessAnalyzerServiceRolePolicy
     arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/acme-org-policy-s3-write

customIAMPolicyTemplate.description:
CustomIAMPolicyTemplate is a YAML (or json) template to produce a custom IAM policy to bind to the workload identity role. The template must compile to a valid AWS policy document.

WF CLI supports a single file include directive in place of a string here when processing a KubeResourcePlan resource using wf apply (or wf validate kuberesourceplan). Use "!file filename" to load the content from a file with the relative path "filename". E.g.:
  Version: "2012-10-17"
  Statement:
    Effect: Allow
    Action: s3:ListBucket
    Resource: arn:aws:s3:::example_bucket

Is a reference to an ExternalIdentity, naming the credential an outbound call authenticates with. The value is the identity's name and the scope it lives at ("my-identity", "my-workspace/my-identity" or "my-workspace/my-env/my-identity"), never credential material itself. Supplying a value resolves it: the identity must exist, you must be allowed to use it for what is calling, and its own kind must be one the definition's identityTypes accepts. A value naming an identity that fails any of those is refused when it is supplied, rather than failing when the call runs. It may only be declared where a definition is able to load an identity. It is refused on a CloudResourcePlan's inputs and outputs, a KubeResourcePlan's inputs, a stack definition's vars, an IntegrationDefinition's paramDefs, and a repo template's inputs, all of which would otherwise receive the reference as a plain string.

Is a reference to a CodeRepo, naming the repository an AI agent works on. The value names the repository as its provider does, "github.com/OWNER/REPO" (e.g. "github.com/appvia/wayfinder"), never a URL or a git credential. Use it on an AI agent's input where the repository is not fixed when the agent is written: the input sets how much of the repository the agent needs (repoAccess) and the branch prefix for its changes (repoBranchPrefix), and whoever starts the conversation supplies the repository. The conversation's spec.sourceContext is built from the value they supply. Supplying a value resolves it: the repository must exist, and the grant in its usableBy must cover the access the input asks for. That grant is checked against the person supplying the repository, not against whoever wrote the agent. The agent is checked separately, against the same repository, when the conversation is created. It may only be declared where a definition is able to load a repository and check that grant. It is refused on a CloudResourcePlan's and a KubeResourcePlan's inputs and outputs, a stack definition's vars, an IntegrationDefinition's paramDefs, and a repo template's inputs: each of those passes its values through as text to Terraform, a Helm chart, a rendered manifest or a scaffolded file, where the reference is only a plain string and no grant over the repository is checked.

When empty, branches are prefixed "wayfinder-ai/". It may be set only on type=coderepo, and is refused on every other type.

kinds.description: KubeResourcePlan is a reusable, versioned template for deploying packaged software — a Helm chart and/or a set of Kubernetes manifests — into the clusters Wayfinder manages. A plan declares the inputs users may supply, the outputs the deployment produces, any cloud workload identity the workload needs, and whether it may be installed once per cluster or many times alongside applications. Users deploy a plan by creating a KubeResource that references it. Plans are published by Wayfinder itself, by the tenant for all workspaces, or within a single workspace.

spec.description: KubeResourcePlanSpec defines the template a kube resource plan deploys, the inputs it accepts and the other plans it depends on.

helm.description: Helm is the Helm chart to install, and the values to install it with.

chartURL.description: ChartURL is the URL to a specific tarball of the helm chart. Must specify either ChartURL, or RepoUrl/RepoRef with ChartName and ChartVersion. Cannot be combined with ChartData (on KubeResourcePlan) or ChartPath (on Stack Components).

repoURL.description: RepoURL is a URL to a helm repository, either HTTP or OCI, e.g. "https://charts.example.com" or "oci://registry.example.com/charts". Must be combined with ChartName and ChartVersion. Cannot be combined with ChartURL, ChartData (on KubeResourcePlan), or ChartPath (on Stack Components). If RepoRef is also provided, this must point to the same URL as the referenced Repository.

repoRef.description: RepoRef is a reference to a Repository resource to use for the chart repo. If provided, the referenced Repository resource must reference the same URL as the RepoUrl field. Must be combined with ChartName and ChartVersion.

chartName.description: ChartName is the name of the chart to install. Required when using RepoUrl/RepoRef. Not required when using ChartURL or ChartData.

chartVersion.description: ChartVersion is the version of the chart to install, e.g. "4.11.2". Required when using RepoUrl/RepoRef. Not required when using ChartURL or ChartData.

valuesTemplate.description:
ValuesTemplate is a template containing the values to use when installing the Helm chart.

WF CLI supports a single file include directive in place of a string here when processing a KubeResourcePlan resource using wf apply (or wf validate kuberesourceplan). Use "!file filename" to load the content from a file with the relative path "filename".

helmTimeout.description: HelmTimeout is the duration to wait for helm install/upgrade operations to complete. If unspecified, the default timeout of 300s will be used. Must be a valid duration string (e.g. "600s", "10m").

skipTests.description: SkipTests will skip execution of any 'helm test' tests defined on the package. Defaults to false.

dryRun.description: DryRun will carry out a helm dry run step before installing or upgrading, to catch problems before anything is changed in the cluster. It is opt-in because a dry run fails for charts whose resources depend on custom resource definitions the chart itself installs. Defaults to false.

releaseName.description: ReleaseName is the name of the release in the cluster. If not specified, the KubeResource name will be used.

chartData.description: ChartData is the raw data of the helm chart. It is a base64 encoded string of a helm chart tar.gz file. Cannot be combined with ChartURL, RepoUrl/RepoRef, or ChartVersion.

additionalValuesFiles.description: AdditionalValuesFiles is a list of additional value files to apply when installing the Helm chart. These will be applied in the order specified after the values template, so can override values from the template. Do not include secret data in these files as they are handled in plain text. These additional files do NOT support templating, all templating should be performed in the ValuesTemplate.

manifests.description: Manifests are Kubernetes manifests to apply to the cluster, applied in the order given.

items.description: Manifest is a single Kubernetes manifest, given as a template, that is applied to the target cluster as part of the deployment.

name.description: Name is an optional name for this manifest. This name is used only for your reference and has no meaning to Wayfinder.

template.description:
