Use "!file filename" to load the content from a file with the relative path "filename". If "!file" is used without a file, the manifest name will be used as the file name.

preInstall.description: PreInstall applies this manifest before the Helm chart is installed, rather than after. Use it for anything the chart itself depends on. Defaults to false.

kubeResourceType.description: KubeResourceType describes what this plan is suitable for, either AppComponent or ClusterWide. If unspecified, AppComponent is assumed.

enumDocs.description: Is a plan installed alongside applications, in their own namespaces. It can be installed many times per cluster, and suits things applications depend on directly, such as a database or a message queue.
Is a plan installed once per cluster, providing cluster-wide capability such as an operator, ingress controller or monitoring agent.

workloadIdentity.description: WorkloadIdentity requests a cloud identity for the workload this plan deploys, so it can access cloud resources without long-lived credentials.

serviceAccountName.description: ServiceAccountName is the name of the service account in the installNamespace which will use this identity in the target cluster.

identityOnly.description:
IdentityOnly will create an identity associated with a cluster with no specific permissions Must specify Role=None if this is true. In AWS:
  - An IAM role is created and associated with a specific Kubernetes service account
  - no inline or attached policies are managed (post creation of the IAM role)
  - It is a "user" responsibility to attach policies to the IAM role
In Azure:
  - The user defined managed identity is created
  - No role definitions or role assignments are created
  - It is a "user" responsibility to create relevant role assignments

kinds.description: Repository is a Helm chart repository that kube resource plans can pull charts from, either an HTTP chart repository or an OCI registry. It records the repository URL, any credentials needed to authenticate to it and any private certificate authority needed to trust it, and lists the charts and versions Wayfinder found there so they can be browsed when building a plan.

spec.description: RepositorySpec defines where a Helm chart repository lives and how to reach it.

description.description: Description is a short description of what this repository holds and when to use it.

url.description: URL is the Helm repository location, including protocol and host, e.g. "https://charts.example.com" or "oci://registry.example.com/charts".

authExternalIdentityRef.description: AuthExternalIdentityRef references a BasicAuth ExternalIdentity that authenticates to the repository with a username and password. The identity's spec.service host must match the repository URL host.

tlsExternalIdentityRef.description: TLSExternalIdentityRef references a TLSClientCert ExternalIdentity providing a client certificate and private key for mutual TLS to the repository. The identity's spec.service host must match the repository URL host.

caBundle.description: CABundle is a PEM-encoded certificate authority bundle used to verify the repository's TLS server certificate, for repositories served from a private or internal CA. It is public trust material, not a credential, so it is held inline rather than in an ExternalIdentity, and is independent of the auth/TLS identity references (it may be set with or without a client-certificate identity).

kinds.description:
Cluster represents a Kubernetes cluster (EKS, AKS, or GKE) that Wayfinder manages as a deployment target for workloads. It records where the cluster lives — the cloud account, region and provider-specific details — which of the cluster's existing ClusterRoles Wayfinder users and deployments may be granted, and whether namespaces are created on demand for the workspaces that share it. Its status reports what Wayfinder can see of the cluster: its health, the connectivity and version of the Wayfinder agent running inside it, and the endpoint used to reach its Kubernetes API.

Clusters can be shared beyond the workspace that owns them; use scope to control which workspaces may deploy to this one.

spec.description: ClusterSpec defines the desired configuration of a Kubernetes cluster.

description.description: Description is a human-readable summary of what this cluster is for.

scope.description: Scope is which other workspaces may use this cluster. By default a cluster can only be used by the workspace that owns it.

destination.description: Destination is the place this target names, e.g. "aws:123456789012:eu-west-2", "k8s:my-workspace/dev/my-cluster:my-namespace" or "srv:vault.internal.corp:8443".

identityRef.description: IdentityRef references the ExternalIdentity Wayfinder authenticates with, for a cloud or service destination, e.g. "my-workspace/aws-nonprod". A kubernetes destination uses clusterRoles instead.

clusterRoles.description: ClusterRoles names the Kubernetes cluster roles anything deployed through this target is bound to, for a kubernetes destination — the access it deploys with. Each entry names a role the cluster owner has allocated to your workspace and the scope to bind it at, e.g. {"clusterRoleName": "cluster-admin", "roleBindingType": "Cluster"}. Left unset, the cluster's default deployment role is used where it has one, and at least one role must be named where it does not. A cloud or service destination uses identityRef instead.

items.description: TargetClusterRole names a Kubernetes ClusterRole the deployment identity is bound to, and the scope it is bound at.

clusterRoleName.description: ClusterRoleName is the name of the ClusterRole in the target cluster, chosen from the roles the cluster owner has allocated to your workspace, e.g. "cluster-admin".

roleBindingType.description: RoleBindingType is the scope to bind at: Namespace (the default) binds in the target's namespace, Cluster binds cluster-wide.

enumDocs.description: Creates RoleBindings in specific namespaces
Creates ClusterRoleBindings for cluster-wide access

cloudResourceName.description: CloudResourceName is the name the cluster has in the cloud provider, e.g. "prod-platform-eks". Leave blank to derive it from the Wayfinder workspace and cluster name.

provider.description: Provider is the managed Kubernetes service this cluster runs on, e.g. "EKS", "AKS" or "GKE".

wfAgent.description: WFAgent configures automatic installation of the Wayfinder agent into this cluster. This is only possible where Wayfinder has direct access to the cluster's Kubernetes API.

autoInstall.description: AutoInstall indicates whether Wayfinder should install the agent for you. This only works where Wayfinder has direct network access to the cluster's Kubernetes API; otherwise install the agent yourself with `wf setup cluster agent`.

namespace.description: Namespace is the Kubernetes namespace to install the agent into, e.g. "wayfinder".

upgrade.description: Upgrade controls whether the agent updates itself to the build Wayfinder installs. Leave it unset for Auto.

enumDocs.description: Has the agent update itself to the build Wayfinder installs. This is what an unset policy means.
Leaves the agent on the build it is running. Wayfinder still reports when it is behind, and a person updates it with `wf setup cluster agent`.

aks.description: AKS holds the Azure-specific details of this cluster. Required when the provider is AKS.

resourceGroup.description: ResourceGroup is the Azure resource group the cluster is deployed into, e.g. "prod-platform-rg".

region.description: Region is the cloud region the cluster resides in, e.g. "eu-west-2" (AWS) or "westeurope" (Azure). It must agree with the region named by destination. Deprecated: superseded by destination, which names the region the cluster is built in. Removed in the next release.

dynamicNamespaces.description: DynamicNamespaces configures whether Wayfinder creates namespaces in this cluster on demand for the environments that deploy to it.

enabled.description: Enabled indicates whether Wayfinder creates namespaces in this cluster on demand.

podSecurityStandard.description: PodSecurityStandard applies Kubernetes Pod Security Standards to the namespaces Wayfinder creates.

enabled.description: Enabled indicates whether Pod Security Standards are enforced on the namespaces Wayfinder creates.

defaultProfile.description: DefaultProfile is the Pod Security Standard profile applied when a namespace does not ask for a specific one, e.g. "baseline" or "restricted".

allowed.description: AllowedProfiles are the Pod Security Standard profiles a namespace may request, e.g. ["baseline", "restricted"].

customNamespacePrefixPattern.description: CustomNamespacePrefixPattern is the prefix to use for dynamic namespaces. If multi-tenancy is enabled, this MUST include {{ .TenantWorkspaceKey }}. No other template variables are supported. Defaults to {{ if .TenantWorkspaceKey }}{{ .TenantWorkspaceKey }}-{{ end }}

additionalLabels.description:
AdditionalLabels are extra Kubernetes labels to put on the namespaces Wayfinder creates. They are applied only at namespace creation — changing them does not affect namespaces that already exist.

The standard 'appvia.io/ownedByWorkspace' (or spec.dynamicNamespaces.customOwnedByLabel if set) is always applied to all dynamic namespaces with a value of the relevant workspace key, in addition to any labels specified here.

customOwnedByLabel.description: CustomOwnedByLabel is the Kubernetes label key that carries the key of the workspace owning a namespace. Wayfinder sets this label on every namespace it creates, and reads it to decide which workspace an existing namespace belongs to. Defaults to appvia.io/ownedByWorkspace.

access.description: Access makes existing ClusterRoles in the cluster available to Wayfinder users via `wf access cluster` and `wf access namespace`, and to deployments made with `wf deploy` and `wf up`.

items.description: ClusterAccessRule makes one or more of the cluster's existing ClusterRoles available to a set of Wayfinder users, for access via `wf access cluster` and `wf access namespace` and for deployments made with `wf up` and `wf deploy`. Exactly one of static or dynamic must be set.

static.description: Static names a single ClusterRole. Set either static or dynamic, not both.

clusterRoleName.description: ClusterRoleName is the name of the ClusterRole in the cluster, e.g. "view" or "edit".

displayName.description: DisplayName provides a user-friendly name shown in CLI/UI selection. This can also be set using an annotation on the ClusterRole of appvia.io/displayName.

description.description: Description provides help text for this role. This can also be set using an annotation on the ClusterRole of appvia.io/description.

dynamic.description: Dynamic matches any number of ClusterRoles by their labels. Set either static or dynamic, not both.

clusterRoleLabels.description: ClusterRoleLabels are the Kubernetes labels a ClusterRole must carry to be matched, e.g. {"appvia.io/wayfinder-access": "true"}. All of them must match.

displayNameLabel.description: DisplayNameAnnotation is the annotation on a matched ClusterRole holding the name to show for it. Defaults to appvia.io/displayName

descriptionLabel.description: DescriptionAnnotation is the annotation on a matched ClusterRole holding the help text to show for it. Defaults to appvia.io/description

roleBindingType.description: RoleBindingType determines how the role is bound to users - either via a ClusterRoleBinding for cluster-wide access, or a RoleBinding in the target namespace for namespace-scoped access

enumDocs.description: Creates RoleBindings in specific namespaces
Creates ClusterRoleBindings for cluster-wide access

subjects.description: Subjects are the users, groups and service accounts allowed to use the role or roles this rule provides. At least one of subjects or wayfinderRoles must be set.

wayfinderRoles.description: WayfinderRoles allow anyone holding the given Wayfinder role at the given scope to use the role or roles this rule provides, without naming them individually in subjects. A grant reaches only where the cluster does: every workspace and environment named here must also appear in spec.scope, "*" requires spec.scope.allWorkspaces, and a tenant-scope grant is only permitted on a cluster shared to all workspaces. At least one of subjects or wayfinderRoles must be set.

items.description:
RoleGrant names a population by the Wayfinder role they hold and where they hold it, so a resource can be granted to "anyone holding this role here" rather than to subjects listed one by one. It is the counterpart to Subject: a Subject says who, a RoleGrant says what someone must be. Membership is read from the roles the caller holds at the time of the request, so a grant follows the role's holders as people join and leave it.

The scope fields are read relative to the scope of the resource being granted, and a field that resource already pins is refused rather than ignored. Where nothing pins them, a scope must be stated, since tenant-scope holders and workspace-scope holders are different populations and neither is a safe default: set workspace (a name, or "*" for any) to mean holders of the role in a workspace, or set tenant to mean holders of it at tenant scope.

role.description: Role is the name of the Wayfinder role whose holders are granted, e.g. "deployer", "viewer" or "workspace.manager".

workspace.description: Workspace is the workspace holders must hold the role in. "*" matches any workspace. It is inert where the granting resource pins a workspace of its own, and is mutually exclusive with tenant.

environment.description: Environment narrows the grant to holders of the role in a single environment. Leave it empty to require the role at workspace scope and nothing narrower, or set "*" to match the role held at workspace scope or in any one environment. It is inert where the granting resource pins an environment of its own, and has no meaning alongside tenant, which names a scope no environment sits under.

tenant.description: Tenant grants to holders of the role at tenant scope, such as "tenant.owner" - a tenant-level role holding rather than one held in any particular workspace, so the two never match the same people. It may only be set where the granting resource reaches the whole tenant, and is mutually exclusive with workspace.

namespaceSelector.description: NamespaceSelector limits the role to namespaces carrying the given Kubernetes labels, and is only valid when roleBindingType is "Namespace". If omitted, the role can be used with any namespace the subject owns. To use it alongside namespaces Wayfinder creates on demand, make sure it matches the labels in dynamicNamespaces.additionalLabels.

matchLabels.description: matchLabels is a map of {key,value} pairs. A single {key,value} in the matchLabels map is equivalent to an element of matchExpressions, whose key field is "key", the operator is "In", and the values array contains only "value". The requirements are ANDed.

matchExpressions.description: matchExpressions is a list of label selector requirements. The requirements are ANDed.

items.description: A label selector requirement is a selector that contains values, a key, and an operator that relates the key and values.

key.description: key is the label key that the selector applies to.

operator.description: operator represents a key's relationship to a set of values. Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists and DoesNotExist.

values.description: values is an array of string values. If the operator is In or NotIn, the values array must be non-empty. If the operator is Exists or DoesNotExist, the values array must be empty. This array is replaced during a strategic merge patch.

defaultDeploymentRole.description: DefaultDeploymentRole is the name of the ClusterRole used for deployments when none is given, e.g. "cluster-admin". This role must be included in the access list, either as a static role or matched by a label selector.

kinds.description:
ClusterRoleBinding grants a Wayfinder user or service account one of the Kubernetes ClusterRoles a cluster makes available, either across the whole cluster or within a single namespace, and optionally only until an expiry time. Wayfinder creates the corresponding Kubernetes binding in the cluster and removes it again when the grant is deleted or expires.

Bindings are normally created for you by `wf access cluster` and `wf access namespace`; the role requested must be one the cluster offers in its access rules, and you must be among the subjects that rule allows.

spec.description: ClusterRoleBindingSpec defines the access being granted: who gets which role, in which cluster and namespace, and for how long.

expiration.description: Expiration is when the granted access stops working and is removed from the cluster. Omit it for access that does not expire.

clusterRoleName.description: ClusterRoleName is the name of the ClusterRole being granted, e.g. "edit". Only roles the cluster makes available through its access rules are accepted.

roleBindingType.description: RoleBindingType is whether the role is granted across the whole cluster, or only within the namespace named below.

enumDocs.description: Creates RoleBindings in specific namespaces
Creates ClusterRoleBindings for cluster-wide access

clusterRef.description: ClusterRef is the cluster this access applies to. Required, including for access granted within a single namespace.

workspace.description: Workspace identifies the workspace in which this item exists. If empty, assume the same workspace as the object holding the reference.

environment.description: Environment identifies the environment in which this item exists.

name.description: Name is the object name of the referenced item

namespace.description: Namespace is the namespace the role is granted in, e.g. "myapp-dev". Only valid when roleBindingType is "Namespace".

subject.description: Subject is the Wayfinder user, group or service account being granted this access.

kinds.description:
Schedule runs one named action on a target resource, over and over, on an interval. Each time the interval elapses Wayfinder starts a run and records it.

You can write one directly — "call this operation every six hours" — and you can also get one for free: a resource that lists what it wants run repeatedly, such as a WebAPI's spec.schedules, has its Schedules maintained for it by the write. Those ones are read-only, and say so: change them where they are declared, and removing the declaration removes the Schedule.

Either way it is the same resource with the same behaviour. There is no second mechanism for a derived schedule, which is what stops the two drifting apart.

spec.description: ScheduleSpec describes what to run and how often.

target.description: Target is the resource the run acts on, e.g. the WebAPI whose operation is being called. It names the kind as well as the resource, because that is what decides how a run is started — Wayfinder has to know it is scheduling a WebAPI to know that starting a run means making a call.

apiGroup.description: APIGroup is the area of our API that this kind is defined by

kind.description: Kind is the kind of the object.

tenant.description: Tenant is the tenant of the object

workspace.description: Workspace unique key for the workspace (empty for tenant/global scoped)

environment.description: Environment is the environment of the object (empty for non-environment-scoped objects)

name.description: Name is the name of the object

version.description: Version is the version of the object. Only relevant if the object implements Versioned interface.

untenanted.description: Untenanted is true if the object is specifically NOT tenant scoped.

action.description: Action names what to run on the target — for a WebAPI, the operation. A target usually offers several, each of which can be scheduled separately and at its own interval, so the action is always named rather than implied.

schedule.description: Schedule is how often to run it, and the inputs to run with.

every.description: Every is how long to wait between runs, e.g. "15m", "1h" or "24h". Pick a value comfortably longer than the run itself takes, and be mindful of what is at the other end: a slow daily report does not want a five-minute interval. The first run happens as soon as the schedule is enabled, and each subsequent run is timed from the start of the previous one, so runs never overlap.

inputs.description:
Inputs are the values to run with, validated against whatever the thing being run declares it accepts — for a WebAPI operation, its own inputs.

A scheduled run has nobody to ask, so anything the run needs has to be settled when the schedule is written: a query parameter, a lookback window, a page size. An operation that requires inputs cannot be scheduled without them.

items.description: TemplatedInput is a named input value, potentially containing template expressions.

name.description: Name matches a ValueDefinition on the associated plan.

value.description: Value is a literal value or template expression, resolved at reconciliation time. Stored as json.RawMessage so non-string types (numbers, bools) survive YAML round-trips without forced quoting. Template expressions like "${{ .Vars.x }}" are stored as JSON strings.

suspend.description: Suspend stops the schedule running without deleting it or losing its history. A run already under way is left to finish.

kinds.description:
Workflow is a reusable template that defines a named set of triggers and the tasks to run when one of them fires. It is the durable definition you author and keep; firing one of its triggers produces a WorkflowInvocation, a single run of the workflow's tasks, which Wayfinder then drives to completion.

Tasks run in parallel by default and each may declare the tasks it depends on, so a workflow can fan out and join. A task calls an HTTP integration operation, holds a conversation with an AI agent, reads a source repository, or runs a Wayfinder CLI command server-side.

spec.description: WorkflowSpec is the authored workflow: workflow-level configuration, the named triggers that start a run, and the tasks to run.

description.description: Description is a short, human-readable description of the workflow.

config.description: Config is static, workflow-level configuration made available to task templates as `.Config.*`. It is fixed by the author and the same for every run of the workflow — a place for shared values such as a budget or an endpoint, distinct from per-run inputs.

files.description:
Files declares the files this workflow's tasks read. A task names one by path, exactly as it would on a command line — `file: Wayfinder.yaml` runs `wf deploy --file Wayfinder.yaml` against these files and nothing else.

A declared file is either carried by the workflow (its content is inlined here, written as "!file <relative path>" and loaded when the workflow is applied) or supplied by a checkout task at run time (no content). Declaring it either way means the spec says what the workflow reads, rather than the answer living in data attached to it.

items.description:
WorkflowFile is one file a workflow's tasks can read.

The path is what a task names. Where the content comes from is declared per file, which is what makes it deterministic: a file carried by the workflow is never quietly replaced by a repository's file of the same name, and a file the repository provides is never quietly served from a stale copy.

path.description: Path is what a task's parameter names, relative to the root of the files the run assembles — e.g. "Wayfinder.yaml", or "plans/db.yaml". Must be a clean relative path: no leading "/" and no ".." components.

kind.description: Kind is what the file must contain, e.g. "StackDefinition" or "CloudResourcePlan". Optional, and checked when the workflow is written: a file that does not parse as its declared kind is an authoring error rather than a failed run at 3am. Leave it empty for content that has no kind — a Helm values file, or a webhook payload.

content.description:
Content is the file itself, carried by the workflow.

Authored as "!file <relative path>" — the Wayfinder include directive, the same one a KubeResourcePlan's manifests use — and replaced with the file's contents when the workflow is applied. The stored workflow therefore holds what its tasks will read, so reviewing the workflow is reviewing the object.

Empty means a checkout task supplies this file. That is the ordinary case for a workflow whose files live in a repository; content is for the case where they do not, or where one file is deliberately pinned to the workflow.

triggers.description: Triggers declares the named conditions that start a run of this workflow. A trigger fires either manually (e.g. `wf invoke workflow`) or automatically when a matching Wayfinder resource event occurs. Each trigger starts its own independent run of the workflow. (Named `triggers` rather than `on` because a bare YAML `on:` key coerces to the boolean true.)

items.description: WorkflowTrigger is a single named trigger on a Workflow. Exactly one trigger flavour is expected per entry (a resource trigger, or a manual trigger).

name.description: Name uniquely identifies the trigger within the workflow, e.g. "nightly". Any trigger starts a run of every task; a task selects a particular trigger by referencing this name in its when condition (`${{ eq .Trigger.Name "nightly" }}`). The run's inputs are also available to task templates keyed under this name as `.On.<name>.*`.

resource.description: Resource is the kind of resource whose events fire this trigger, e.g. "StackInstance". Set it together with Event to fire the trigger automatically on a matching resource event.

event.description: Event is the resource event that fires this trigger, e.g. "Created". Set it together with Resource.

when.description: When is an optional condition gating the fire: a `${{ }}` template expression evaluated against the triggering resource. The trigger fires only when it renders to "true"; combine conditions with `and`/`or` in one expression, e.g. `${{ and (eq .Resource.spec.tier "prod") (ne .Resource.metadata.name "test") }}`.

manual.description: Manual declares this trigger as manually fireable, with an optional input schema validated against the run subresource's supplied inputs.

inputs.description: Inputs is the schema of the inputs this trigger accepts (name, type and whether each is required). The values supplied when the trigger is fired are validated against it, and are available to task templates as `.Inputs.*`.

items.description: ValueDefinition defines the shape of an input/output/data value

name.description: Name of the variable

description.description: Description iof the value

secret.description: Secret indicates if the value is a secret and should be protected

type.description: Type is the type of the value

enumDocs.description: Is a string type
Is a number type (integer or floating point)
Is a boolean type
Is a list type of strings
Is a list type of numbers
Is a list type of booleans
Is a map type of strings
Is a map type of numbers
Is a map type of booleans
Is an arbitrary JSON type, used to represent any complex input/output that isn't better represented by the other types. Note that no validation is possible for a plain JSON input.

Is a reference to an ExternalIdentity, naming the credential an outbound call authenticates with. The value is the identity's name and the scope it lives at ("my-identity", "my-workspace/my-identity" or "my-workspace/my-env/my-identity"), never credential material itself. Supplying a value resolves it: the identity must exist, you must be allowed to use it for what is calling, and its own kind must be one the definition's identityTypes accepts. A value naming an identity that fails any of those is refused when it is supplied, rather than failing when the call runs. It may only be declared where a definition is able to load an identity. It is refused on a CloudResourcePlan's inputs and outputs, a KubeResourcePlan's inputs, a stack definition's vars, an IntegrationDefinition's paramDefs, and a repo template's inputs, all of which would otherwise receive the reference as a plain string.

Is a reference to a CodeRepo, naming the repository an AI agent works on. The value names the repository as its provider does, "github.com/OWNER/REPO" (e.g. "github.com/appvia/wayfinder"), never a URL or a git credential. Use it on an AI agent's input where the repository is not fixed when the agent is written: the input sets how much of the repository the agent needs (repoAccess) and the branch prefix for its changes (repoBranchPrefix), and whoever starts the conversation supplies the repository. The conversation's spec.sourceContext is built from the value they supply. Supplying a value resolves it: the repository must exist, and the grant in its usableBy must cover the access the input asks for. That grant is checked against the person supplying the repository, not against whoever wrote the agent. The agent is checked separately, against the same repository, when the conversation is created. It may only be declared where a definition is able to load a repository and check that grant. It is refused on a CloudResourcePlan's and a KubeResourcePlan's inputs and outputs, a stack definition's vars, an IntegrationDefinition's paramDefs, and a repo template's inputs: each of those passes its values through as text to Terraform, a Helm chart, a rendered manifest or a scaffolded file, where the reference is only a plain string and no grant over the repository is checked.

optional.description: Optional is true when no value need be supplied: the object declaring it can be saved, and switched on where it has a switch, without one. An unanswered optional value reads as its defaultValue when one is set, and as nothing otherwise. Whether whoever uses the object may supply it later is for that object to say.

minimum.description: Minimum is the minimum numerical value of the variable if a number/float

maximum.description: Maximum is the maximum numerical value of the variable if a number/float

minLength.description: MinLength is the minimum number or length of the variable if a string

maxLength.description: MaxLength is the maximum number or length of the variable if a string

minItems.description: MinItems is the minimum number of items in the variable if a list or map

maxItems.description: MaxItems is the maximum number of items in the variable if a list or map

pattern.description: Pattern is the pattern of the variable if a string. For list(string) and map(string), this is applied to each individual value in the list or map.

enum.description: Enum is the list of valid values for a string or number (or the values of lists/maps of those types). Ignored for other types.

requiredKeys.description: RequiredKeys is the list of required keys for a map variable. Ignored for other types.

refType.description: RefType describes that this value is a reference to another Wayfinder resource. When set, the value is validated to be the name of an existing resource of the given kind, optionally filtered by field constraints.

kind.description: Kind is the Wayfinder resource kind being referenced (e.g. "ExternalIdentity", "CodeRepo")

filter.description: Filter is an optional set of dot-path field matchers on the referenced resource. Keys are dot-paths (e.g. "spec.cloud"), values are the expected string match. All entries must match (AND semantics).

identityTypes.description: IdentityTypes lists the ExternalIdentity types this input accepts, e.g. ["BearerToken"] for an API that authenticates with a bearer token, or ["BasicAuth", "BearerToken"] where either will do. A value naming an identity of any other type is refused when it is supplied, rather than failing when the call runs. Leaving it empty accepts any identity type that can authenticate an outbound call. It may be set only on type=externalidentity, and is refused on every other type.

repoAccess.description: RepoAccess is how much of the repository the agent needs: "read" to clone and read it, "propose" to also commit to a fresh branch and open a pull request, or "proposeWorkflows" to also change the repository's CI workflow definitions. When empty, Wayfinder uses "read". Whoever supplies a repository must themselves be granted at least this much of it, and so must the agent, or the conversation is refused when it is created. It may be set only on type=coderepo, and is refused on every other type.

repoBranchPrefix.description: RepoBranchPrefix is prepended to the name of the branch the agent's changes are committed to, e.g. "wayfinder-ai/cost-control/". When empty, branches are prefixed "wayfinder-ai/". Set it so branch protection or CODEOWNERS rules in the repository match every branch this agent opens; whoever starts the conversation cannot change it. It may be set only on type=coderepo, and is refused on every other type.

schema.description: Schema provides additional guidance as to the shape of the value when type=json.

tasks.description: Tasks is the set of tasks to run, keyed by task name. Tasks run in parallel by default; a task that declares dependsOn waits for those tasks first. Any trigger starts a run of all the tasks — use a task's when condition to run it only in certain cases (for example only for a particular trigger).

values.description: WorkflowTask is a single task in a workflow, identified by its key in the workflow's tasks map.

action.description: Action is the "<integration>/<type>/<...>" slash-path identifying the work to perform: the first segment names the owning integration, the second selects the kind of thing to run, and the rest names it. "<integration>/webapi/<webapi>/<operation>" runs an HTTP integration action; "ai/agent/<name>" runs a conversation with the named AIAgent, and its structured result becomes the task's output — name a tenant agent as "ai/agent/<name>" and one a workspace owns as "ai/agent/<workspace>/<name>" or "ai/agent/<workspace>/<environment>/<name>", where the workspace must be the workflow's own; "ai/agent/wayfinder/<name>" runs one of the agents Wayfinder ships, which any workflow may name; "wf/<command>/<subcommand>..." runs a Wayfinder CLI command server-side; "checkout/github.com/<owner>/<repo>" reads the named source repository into the run's files.

checkout.description: Checkout configures how much of a "checkout/github.com/<owner>/<repo>" task's repository to read — the ref and the subdirectory. Which repository is the action's own business. Rejected on any other action.

workspace.description:
Workspace is no longer used: the action names the repository, whichever workspace owns it. Saving a task that sets it is refused.

Deprecated: name the repository in the action, as "checkout/github.com/OWNER/REPO".

ref.description: Ref is the branch, tag or commit to read. Empty reads the repository's default branch. Whatever is given, the commit it resolves to is recorded on the run — the branch may move, but what ran does not.

subdirectory.description: Subdirectory reads only a subtree of the repository, and makes that subtree the root of the run's files: with "stacks/payments", a task reads "Wayfinder.yaml" for the file the repository holds at "stacks/payments/Wayfinder.yaml". Must be a clean relative path — no ".." components and no leading "/". Empty reads the whole repository.

dependsOn.description: DependsOn lists the names of tasks that must succeed before this task is scheduled. A task whose dependencies are all skipped is skipped; a task that joins several branches runs as soon as its un-skipped dependencies succeed. A dependency that failed normally takes this task down with it, unless that dependency declared continueOnFailure.

continueOnFailure.description:
ContinueOnFailure marks this task as best-effort: if it fails, the tasks that depend on it still run, and the run as a whole still succeeds. Use it for a step whose failure is not worth abandoning the rest of the workflow for — inviting a user, posting a notification, tagging a resource.

The failure is not hidden: the task still reports as Failed with its reason, the run's message names every tolerated failure, and a dependent task can see what happened via `${{ .Tasks.<name>.failed }}`, `.phase`, and `.error.*` — so it can react (report it, take the other path) rather than only carry on.

when.description: When optionally gates whether this task runs: a `${{ }}` template expression evaluated against the run context just before the task would be dispatched. The task runs only when it renders to "true"; otherwise it is skipped (and tasks that depend solely on it are skipped in turn). Use it to run a task only in certain cases, for example only for a particular trigger (`${{ eq .Trigger.Name "nightly" }}`) or based on an upstream task's output.

inputs.description: Inputs provides templated values for this task, resolved live at dispatch time against the run context (`.Inputs.*`, `.Tasks.<name>.output.*`).

items.description: TemplatedInput is a named input value, potentially containing template expressions.

name.description: Name matches a ValueDefinition on the associated plan.

value.description: Value is a literal value or template expression, resolved at reconciliation time. Stored as json.RawMessage so non-string types (numbers, bools) survive YAML round-trips without forced quoting. Template expressions like "${{ .Vars.x }}" are stored as JSON strings.

with.description: With provides a "wf/..." task's command parameters as named fields — each key is one of the command's own flags (or the reserved "name"/"args" positionals), typed exactly as the CLI defines it, and validated against the CLI's command schema when the workflow is written. Values are templated like Inputs. Rejected on other task types, whose parameters are their Inputs.

ai.description: AI carries the settings that apply only to an "ai/agent" task: where the conversation is created, the source repository the agent works against, and the model and effort to run it on. Ignored by every other task type.

placement.description: Placement names where this task's conversation is created. Defaults to where the run is.

workspace.description: Workspace is the workspace the conversation is created in, e.g. "kteam".

environment.description: Environment is the environment within that workspace the conversation is created in, e.g. "dev". Naming one without a workspace is refused: an environment belongs to a workspace, and the conversation needs both.

sourceContext.description: SourceContext binds the conversation to a source repository, so the agent's file tools read and write that repository. Required when the agent declares requiresSourceContext. Whether the agent may propose a change is declared on the source context itself, not here.

kind.description: Kind identifies the source kind. Only "github" is meaningful for a workflow: a hands-off run has no client to serve a local filesystem.

repo.description: Repo names the repository the agent reads from, as "github.com/OWNER/REPO", e.g. "github.com/appvia/wayfinder", or a ${{ }} template that renders to one.

branch.description: Branch is the branch to read from. Empty resolves the CodeRepo's default branch, the same way it does for an interactive conversation.

subdirectory.description: Subdirectory constrains the agent's file tools, and any file it proposes, to a subtree of the repository. Must be a clean relative path — no ".." components and no absolute path. Empty means the repository root.

propose.description: Propose, when set, lets the task's agent change the repository: its file tools may write as well as read, and it may commit those changes and open a pull request. Its presence IS the grant, so a task that omits it dispatches an agent that can only read.

branchPrefix.description: BranchPrefix is prepended to the name of the branch the agent's changes are committed to. Must be a clean relative path, and conventionally ends with "/" so the branches group under it — e.g. "wayfinder-ai/cost-control/". Empty uses Wayfinder's own default prefix.

followPullRequest.description:
FollowPullRequest keeps the task's agent available after it opens a pull request: someone commenting on that pull request, or reviewing it, puts the agent back to work on it. The agent reads the pull request itself and decides what to do — nothing anyone wrote there is passed to it. Without this the run ends at the pull request, and a review left on it reaches nobody.

The agent must declare spec.supportsFollowPullRequests.

model.description: Model runs this task's conversation on a model other than the one its agent declares, named as "<provider>:<model>" — "anthropic:sonnet-5", say, for the one task in a workflow that needs the harder thinking. It may be a `${{ }}` template, e.g. "${{ .Config.model }}", so the choice can live in the workflow's own configuration.

effort.description: Effort is how hard the model should think before answering in this task's conversation, overriding what its agent asks for: one of none, low, medium, high, xhigh or max. A level the model cannot reach is clamped to the nearest it can. It may be a `${{ }}` template, like the fields above.

enabled.description:
Enabled toggles whether this workflow's triggers fire. Omitted means enabled — an explicit false is required to turn a workflow off, so a workflow written before the toggle existed keeps running. Workflows installed from the catalogue start disabled; turn them on once configured.

Turning one on is checked: everything the workflow names — the agents its tasks call, the web APIs they call, and the integrations behind those — must exist and be enabled. Its inputs are NOT checked here: they are supplied when it is invoked, and the run is where a missing value is refused.

suggestedRoles.description: SuggestedRoles names the roles a tenant should grant this workflow so it can run. A workflow acts as itself, so one whose tasks run Wayfinder commands can do nothing until it holds a role that allows them. The author declares what it needs here (e.g. ["tenant.manager"]); the catalogue and the workflow's readiness surface them. Each must be a role a tenant user can grant.

kinds.description: DataType describes the shape of data returned by an integration, as a JSON Schema that the response is validated against before it is stored, plus the fields within it that should be searchable. Data types are entirely optional - a response with no data type named for it is stored as-is, without validation.

spec.description: DataTypeSpec defines the schema and searchable fields for a data type.

description.description: Description is a human-readable description of what this data type represents.

indexedFields.description: IndexedFields are the field paths within the data that are made searchable, so components can be filtered on those values, e.g. ["id", "owner.team"].

schema.description: Schema is the JSON Schema that data of this type is validated against. Any valid JSON Schema is accepted; draft-07 is recommended, e.g. {"type": "object", "properties": {"id": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["id"]}.

kinds.description: Environment is a deployment stage within a workspace, e.g. dev, staging or production. Deployments are made into an environment, the variable and secret hierarchy can be given per-environment values, and access is granted per environment - so a team can be free to deploy into dev while production stays restricted.

spec.description: EnvironmentSpec defines the desired configuration of an environment.

description.description: Description is a human-readable description of what this environment is for.

slug.description: Slug is a short (max 8 character), immutable identifier for this environment, unique within its workspace, e.g. "prod". It is generated from the environment name on creation if not supplied. It is not needed for everyday use - reference the environment by its name - but is available for length-constrained naming, such as cloud resource names in templates, where it is exposed as .EnvironmentSlug.

kinds.description: Group is a named collection of users and service accounts, used to keep permission management manageable: grant roles to the group once, then control who holds those roles by changing its membership. Groups can also be nested as members of other groups.

spec.description: GroupSpec defines the membership and management of a group.

managers.description: Managers are the subjects allowed to change this group's membership. They do not need to be members themselves, and being a manager does NOT convey membership - so a manager does not receive the roles granted to the group. If empty, only tenant owners can change the membership.

description.description: Description is a human-readable description of what this group is for.

members.description: Members are the users, service accounts and other groups that belong to this group, and so receive every role granted to it.

kinds.description: Invite is an invitation for someone to join a tenant, addressed to an email address and carrying the roles and workspace memberships they will be granted when they accept. The invitation link is emailed to them and is valid until the invite expires; revoking an invite means deleting it.

spec.description: InviteSpec defines who is being invited and what they are granted on acceptance.

email.description: Email is the email address the invitation is sent to, e.g. "alex@acme.com".

roles.description: Roles are the names of the Wayfinder roles granted when the invite is accepted. At least one is required, e.g. ["tenant.member"].

workspaceRoles.description: WorkspaceRoles are workspace-scoped roles granted when the invite is accepted, each entry naming one workspace and the roles granted in it, e.g. workspace "team-a" with role "workspace.member". Use this to invite someone straight into a workspace instead of granting them access afterwards.

items.description: InviteWorkspaceRoles is a set of workspace-scoped roles granted in one workspace when an invite is accepted.

workspace.description: Workspace is the name of the workspace the roles are granted in, e.g. "team-a". The workspace must already exist in the tenant.

roles.description: Roles are the names of the Wayfinder roles granted in the workspace, e.g. ["workspace.member"]. Each role must be valid at workspace scope.

workspaces.description: Workspaces are the names of the workspaces to add the invited person to. They are added to each named workspace's members group on acceptance.

expiresAt.description: ExpiresAt is when the invitation stops being usable. After this point the invite reads as expired and a new one must be sent.

invitedBy.description: InvitedBy is the username of the person who created the invite.

message.description: Message is an optional personal note included in the invitation email.

autoJoin.description: AutoJoin indicates the person was admitted automatically because their email domain is allowed for this tenant, rather than being invited by name. Set by Wayfinder.

scope.description: Scope is how far the granted access reaches. Only tenant owners and admins can create invites.

tokenID.description: TokenID identifies the invitation link that is currently valid. The link itself is only ever emailed to the invited person and is never stored, so it cannot be retrieved; resending the invite issues a new link and invalidates the previous one.

tenant.description: Tenant is the tenant the invite belongs to. It is filled in only when invites are listed across tenants, for example when showing someone every invitation waiting for them, and is empty otherwise.

kinds.description: Label is one of the labels in use across a tenant. Its name is either a label key on its own, e.g. "team", or a key and value together separated by a colon, e.g. "team:platform". Labels appear automatically as soon as any resource is labelled, so you can list what is already in use; creating one explicitly lets you offer a key or value before anything carries it, and deleting one tidies a value that is no longer wanted. A key cannot be deleted while values still exist under it. Labels carry no configuration of their own beyond their name and metadata.

RoleBinding grants one or more Wayfinder roles to a user, group or service account. How far the granted access reaches is decided by where the binding is created rather than by what it is: create it at system, tenant, workspace or environment level and the roles apply there. This one kind covers every scope, replacing the four scope-specific role-binding kinds that remain only for existing configuration.

spec.description: RoleBindingSpec defines who is granted which roles by a role binding.

roles.description: Roles are the names of the Wayfinder roles granted to the subject, e.g. ["workspace.admin"].

subject.description: Subject is the single user, group or service account the roles are granted to.

kinds.description: ServiceAccount is a non-human account for automating Wayfinder from CI pipelines, scripts and other external systems. A service account can be granted roles in the same way as a user, and authenticates using one or more credentials, each represented by a ServiceAccountCredential. A service account created without a workspace can be granted access across the whole tenant; one created within a workspace can only be used within that workspace.

spec.description: ServiceAccountSpec defines the desired state of a service account.

description.description: Description provides a short summary of what this service account is used for, e.g. "Deploys team-a services from GitHub Actions".

kinds.description: ServiceAccountCredential is a single way for a service account to authenticate to Wayfinder. A service account can have several credentials at once, allowing new credentials to be issued and old ones removed without interrupting automation. Deleting a credential immediately revokes it.

spec.description: ServiceAccountCredentialSpec defines a credential for a service account.

serviceAccount.description: ServiceAccount is the name of the service account this credential authenticates. It must exist in the same workspace (or, for a service account without a workspace, the same tenant) as this credential.

method.description: Method is how this credential authenticates: "Token" for a Wayfinder-issued secret token, or "Federated" for an inbound OIDC trust described by the federated block.

enumDocs.description: Authenticates with a Wayfinder-issued secret token. The token is returned once when the credential is created and remains valid until the credential is deleted or its expiry passes.

Authenticates by exchanging a short-lived OIDC identity token from a trusted external issuer (for example GitHub Actions or another cloud) for a Wayfinder API token. No secret is stored: the trust is described entirely by the federated block.

federated.description: Federated describes the inbound OIDC trust for a credential with method "Federated". It must be set for that method and must be empty for any other.

issuer.description: Issuer is the OIDC issuer that must have signed the presented token, matched exactly against the token's "iss" claim. It must be an https URL with no query or fragment; OIDC discovery is performed against it at exchange time.

subject.description: Subject is matched against the token's "sub" claim. It is an exact match unless it ends with a single "*", which makes it a prefix match (for example "repo:acme/app:*"). The "*" is only valid as the final character and the prefix before it must be at least eight characters.

audiences.description: Audiences are the accepted values for the token's "aud" claim; at least one must match. When omitted it is defaulted at creation time to this instance's canonical Wayfinder audience for the tenant, which is also the audience the workload must request.

claims.description: Claims are additional token claims that must all be present and exactly equal to the given values, for example pinning GitHub's rename-proof "repository_owner_id".

expiresAt.description: ExpiresAt is the time at which this credential stops being accepted for authentication. If unset, the credential remains valid until it is deleted.

clientID.description: ClientID is the fully-qualified, non-secret client identifier for a "Token" credential: tenant:service-account:credential (or tenant:workspace:service-account:credential). It is set when the credential is created so client tools have a canonical value to read; present it with the client secret to the token endpoint. Empty for "Federated" credentials.

kinds.description: Workspace is a team's or project's own area within a tenant, and the main unit of isolation below the tenant itself. It owns the resources created in it, holds the environments those resources are deployed into, and is the level most access is granted at - so one team's workspace stays separate from another's.

spec.description: WorkspaceSpec defines the desired configuration of a workspace.

slug.description: Slug is a short (max 8 character), immutable identifier for this workspace, unique within the tenant, e.g. "plat". It is generated from the workspace name on creation if not supplied. It is not needed for everyday use - reference the workspace by its name - but is available for length-constrained naming, such as cloud resource names in templates, where it is exposed as .WorkspaceSlug.

type.description: Type is what this workspace is used for. Defaults to "standard" if not given.

enumDocs.description: Is an ordinary workspace belonging to an application team, and is what a workspace is unless stated otherwise.

description.description: Description is a human-readable description of what this workspace is for.

kinds.description:
CodeRepo is a catalogue entry for a single source code repository that Wayfinder can reach, naming the repository and the source control connection it is reached through. Registering a repository as a CodeRepo checks once that Wayfinder really can reach it, and gives other resources — such as a SourceProposal — a stable name to refer to it by, so they do not each have to repeat the connection details. A CodeRepo records what the repository is and whether it is still reachable; it does not itself change anything in the repository.

A repository is owned by exactly one workspace, which is required: there is no tenant-level repository. To let another workspace use it, grant that workspace in spec.usableBy — the repository stays where it is, and anything in the other workspace names it as GitHub does, "github.com/OWNER/REPO".

spec.description: CodeRepoSpec defines the repository this catalogue entry refers to and the source control connection it is reached through. Exactly one connection reference must be set.

githubOrgRef.description: GitHubOrgRef names the GitHub organization connection this repository is reached through.

name.description: Name is the name of the GitHubOrg, e.g. "appvia".

repo.description: Repo is the repository name on its own, without the owning organization, e.g. "wayfinder". The organization comes from the connection.

defaultBranch.description: DefaultBranch overrides the branch Wayfinder treats as this repository's main working branch, e.g. "main". Leave it empty to use the default branch reported by the provider, which is published in the status.

displayName.description: DisplayName is a friendlier name to show for this repository in place of its repository name, e.g. "Wayfinder Platform".

provision.description: Provision creates the repository on GitHub if it is not there already, e.g. a new repository for a stack. Leave it false to catalogue a repository that already exists. The repository is created once and never again: one deleted on GitHub afterwards is reported as orphaned rather than made a second time.

visibility.description: Visibility is the desired repository visibility when Provision is set: "public", "private" or "internal". Empty defaults to private. Ignored for a linked (non-provisioned) repository.

description.description: Description is an optional repository description applied when Provision creates the repository. Ignored for a linked repository.

githubAccess.description: GitHubAccess names the GitHub teams and users in the organization given GitHub's Admin or Write role on the repository when Provision creates it, so whoever asked for it can work in it without anyone adding them on GitHub. Each name is checked against the organization first: the repository is not created while any name is a team or user the organization does not have, or while the Wayfinder GitHub App cannot read the organization's teams and members (it needs Members: read). Access is granted once, when the repository is created: changing it afterwards changes nothing on GitHub. Ignored for a linked repository.

admin.description: Admin names who gets GitHub's Admin role: everything Write allows, plus changing the repository's settings, branch protection and who else has access, and deleting it.

teams.description: Teams are the slugs of teams in the organization, as they appear in each team's URL, e.g. "accounts-payable" for github.com/orgs/acme/teams/accounts-payable.

users.description: Users are the GitHub logins of members of the organization, e.g. "octocat". Case does not matter.

write.description: Write names who gets GitHub's Write role: they can clone the repository, push branches, and open and review pull requests, but cannot change its settings.

teams.description: Teams are the slugs of teams in the organization, as they appear in each team's URL, e.g. "accounts-payable" for github.com/orgs/acme/teams/accounts-payable.

users.description: Users are the GitHub logins of members of the organization, e.g. "octocat". Case does not matter.

usableBy.description:
UsableBy lists who may use this repository through Wayfinder, and how far. Each entry names either a subject or a Wayfinder role held at a scope, plus the access it is granted. Being able to SEE a repository is a separate question, decided by Wayfinder roles; this decides who may act on it — obtain a git credential for it, propose changes to it, or have Wayfinder read and write it on their behalf.

An empty list grants nobody anything: a repository nobody is listed on can be catalogued and read as an entry, and no work can be done against it.

items.description: CodeRepoUsableBy grants access over a repository to a grantee. The grantee is either an explicit subject or a Wayfinder role held at a scope — exactly one of subject or role must be set.

subject.description: Subject is the user, service account, group, AI agent, workflow or webhook this grant is for. Exactly one of subject or role must be set.

role.description: Role grants access to any subject holding a Wayfinder role at a scope, evaluated from the roles the caller holds at the time of the request. Name the workspace those holders must hold the role in — "*" for every workspace, e.g. `{role: workspace.member, workspace: "*"}` to offer a template to the whole tenant — or set tenant to grant to holders of a tenant-level role. Leave the workspace out to grant only within the workspace that owns the repository. Exactly one of subject or role must be set.
Role is the name of the Wayfinder role whose holders are granted, e.g. "deployer", "viewer" or "workspace.manager".

workspace.description: Workspace is the workspace holders must hold the role in. "*" matches any workspace. It is inert where the granting resource pins a workspace of its own, and is mutually exclusive with tenant.

environment.description: Environment narrows the grant to holders of the role in a single environment. Leave it empty to require the role at workspace scope and nothing narrower, or set "*" to match the role held at workspace scope or in any one environment. It is inert where the granting resource pins an environment of its own, and has no meaning alongside tenant, which names a scope no environment sits under.

tenant.description: Tenant grants to holders of the role at tenant scope, such as "tenant.owner" - a tenant-level role holding rather than one held in any particular workspace, so the two never match the same people. It may only be set where the granting resource reaches the whole tenant, and is mutually exclusive with workspace.

access.description: Access is how far this grantee may go: "read" to clone and fetch, "write" to also push and open pull requests, or "write-workflows" to also change CI workflow definitions.

enumDocs.description: Clones and fetches the repository and reads its CI results — which workflow run failed, which check is red, and what has been deployed.
Additionally pushes branches, opens pull requests and comments on them.

Additionally pushes changes to CI workflow definitions under .github/workflows, which GitHub refuses at "write" alone. It is a level of its own because such a push changes what CI runs — on a self-hosted runner, what runs on your own machines.

kinds.description: GitHubOrg is a connection between Wayfinder and a GitHub organization, established by installing the Wayfinder GitHub App into that organization. The connection lets Wayfinder read and raise changes against the repositories the organization has shared with the App, and it lists those repositories in its status so you can see exactly what Wayfinder can reach. Register an individual repository as a CodeRepo to refer to it elsewhere in Wayfinder. A GitHubOrg is held at tenant level and can be used by every workspace in the tenant.

spec.description: GitHubOrgSpec defines which GitHub organization this connection is to.

organization.description: Organization is the GitHub organization or personal account this connection is to, given as its GitHub login, e.g. "appvia". It must be one of the accounts the install grant covers that you are allowed to connect.

installGrant.description: InstallGrant is the short-lived token Wayfinder issues when you return from authorising the Wayfinder GitHub App on GitHub. It lists the accounts the App is installed on that you can see, and says which you may connect: an organization you are an owner of, your own personal account, or an installation you asked an owner to approve. Supply it when creating a connection, or when updating one to reconnect it to the installation the grant holds for the same organization after the App was installed again. It is consumed and never stored. The same organization may be connected to several tenants, once in each. The GitHub connect flow supplies it automatically.

kinds.description:
RepoTemplate registers an upstream repository as a scaffolding template. The template's definition — name, description, language, inputs and skeleton location — lives inside the template repository as a wayfinder-template.yaml manifest, so a template is versioned together with its content. Wayfinder keeps a copy of that manifest, refreshed from the source, for catalogue listings and input forms; scaffolding renders the skeleton tree with a user's inputs and pushes the result as the initial commit of a newly-created repository.

The source is either a CodeRepo (private repositories, accessed through the GitHub App) or a public https git URL (community templates, read anonymously). Exactly one must be set.

spec.description: RepoTemplateSpec defines where the template is read from and how it is classified in the catalogue.

codeRepoRef.description: CodeRepoRef names the repository holding the template, e.g. "github.com/appvia/templates" — use it for a template repository read through the GitHub App, which is the only way to reach a private one. It must be registered with Wayfinder, and the workspace that owns it must have shared it in its spec.usableBy. Exactly one of codeRepoRef or url must be set.

url.description: URL is a public https git URL holding the template, cloned anonymously (read-only) — for community/starter templates outside a connected org. Exactly one of codeRepoRef or url must be set.

ref.description: Ref is the branch or tag to read the template from. Empty means the repository's default branch.

path.description: Path is the directory within the repository containing the template's wayfinder-template.yaml manifest (and, relative to it, the skeleton files). Empty means the repository root, allowing one repository to host several templates in subdirectories.

displayName.description: DisplayName is an optional human-friendly label for UI. The synced manifest's name (status.manifest.name) is preferred when present.

category.description: Category is a cloud-agnostic taxonomy entry (e.g. "service", "library", "pipeline") classifying what this template scaffolds, drawn from the curated list served by the catalogue. Set by the platform team when registering the template. The catalogue filters and searches on it. Free-form (validated for format only); the curated list is a picker convenience. Language/framework and other free-form axes are metadata.labels, not this.

kinds.description: Stack is a named, deployable unit of application and infrastructure within a workspace, and the lasting identity that every deployment of it belongs to. The stack's contents — its components, variables and secrets — are described in a Wayfinder.yaml, which can be held in an associated code repository. Deploying that definition into an environment with `wf deploy` or `wf up` produces a StackInstance; the Stack itself carries the name, description and repository the deployments share.

spec.description: StackSpec defines the desired configuration of a stack.

description.description: Description is a human-readable description of the stack.

repoRef.description: RepoRef optionally associates this Stack with the CodeRepo that hosts its Wayfinder.yaml; when set, the UI treats that repository as the canonical location and offers AI-assisted editing against it via Pull Requests. Name the repository as "github.com/OWNER/REPO", e.g. "github.com/acme/payments". A repository another workspace owns has to have been granted write to this one, since a linked repository is one the stack opens pull requests against.

repoPath.description: RepoPath is the path within that repository, relative to its root, where the stack's Wayfinder.yaml lives, e.g. "stacks/payments". Empty means the repository root.

repoFile.description: RepoFile is the name of the stack's file within repoPath, e.g. "prod.yaml" for a stack defined by "stacks/payments/prod.yaml". Empty means "Wayfinder.yaml".

repoBranch.description: RepoBranch is the branch holding the version of this stack's Wayfinder.yaml everyone should edit, e.g. "release". Empty means the repository's default branch.

createdFrom.description: CreatedFrom records the template this stack was scaffolded from — the template reference, the pinned template commit that was rendered, and the inputs supplied at scaffold time. It is provenance only: it is never reconciled and is immutable once set. For a stack scaffolded into an existing repository (which lands as a pull request), this records intent at creation time; the checked-in wayfinder-stack.yaml materialises when that pull request merges.

apiGroup.description: APIGroup is the API group of the source the stack was created from (for a template, the source control API group).

kind.description: Kind is the kind of the source the stack was created from, e.g. RepoTemplate.

name.description: Name is the name of the source the stack was created from, e.g. the RepoTemplate name.

commit.description: Commit is the pinned template commit that was rendered to scaffold the stack, so the origin is reproducible.

inputs.description: Inputs are the values supplied to the template at scaffold time.
